verdicts.claim: SqliteConnector.h documents Exception::SqlOperationFailed for countTableRows on an unknown table, but the implementation actually throws Exception::IllegalArgument.
verdicts.evidence: Confirmed in the current source. src/openms/include/OpenMS/FORMAT/SqliteConnector.h:80 read `/// @throws Exception::SqlOperationFailed if table is unknown`. The real path: src/openms/source/FORMAT/SqliteConnector.cpp:107-108 builds `SELECT count(*) FROM "<name>";` and hands it to Internal::SqliteHelper::prepareStatement, which at src/openms/source/FORMAT/SqliteConnector.cpp:166-171 throws `Exception::IllegalArgument` whenever sqlite3_prepare_v2 returns anything but SQLITE_OK -- and an absent table makes SQLite reject the statement at prepare time, never reaching a step. SqlOperationFailed is only thrown further down at src/openms/source/FORMAT/SqliteConnector.cpp:111-114, i.e. for a successfully prepared query that yields no row or a NULL count (locked/broken DB), not for an unknown table. The class test already pins the real behaviour: src/tests/class_tests/openms/source/SqliteConnector_test.cpp:106 `TEST_EXCEPTION(Exception::IllegalArgument, conn.countTableRows("UNKNOWN"))`. No caller depends on the documented type -- the single in-tree caller, src/openms/source/FORMAT/OSWFile.cpp:2639 in OSWFile::readTransitions_, does not catch anything around the call -- so the mismatch is documentation only, with no behavioural bug behind it.
verdicts.change: Documentation corrected in the one file I own (src/openms/include/OpenMS/FORMAT/SqliteConnector.h:79-83): the single `@throws Exception::SqlOperationFailed if table is unknown` line is replaced by two `@throws` lines that name IllegalArgument for the unknown-table case (with the reason: the query is rejected already at prepare time, which is this class's generic bad-SQL error) and keep SqlOperationFailed for the remaining case it is genuinely thrown in (prepared query yields no row or a NULL count). Deliberately did NOT translate the exception in SqliteConnector.cpp: that file belongs to group sqmass-a, and it would also be a silent API change contradicting the existing test expectation at SqliteConnector_test.cpp:106. No test edit was needed -- SqliteConnector_test.cpp:106 is already the runnable check that pins the now-correctly-documented contract, and SqliteConnector_test.cpp:140-141 pins SqlOperationFailed for the constructor, which the header documents correctly at line 59.
verdicts.regression_risk: None. Comment-only change inside a Doxygen block; no declaration, signature, default argument or preprocessor condition touched, so neither the ABI nor any generated code changes. The only observable effect is Doxygen output for SqliteConnector::countTableRows.

verdicts.claim: Chunks::add records {previous_end, spec_.size(), is_sorted} without requiring the spectrum to have grown, so a shrunken spectrum yields a chunk with start > end that sortByPositionPresorted feeds to std::stable_sort/std::inplace_merge.
verdicts.evidence: The claim holds on the current source. Before the fix src/openms/include/OpenMS/KERNEL/MSSpectrum.h:80 read `chunks_.emplace_back((chunks_.empty() ? 0 : chunks_.back().end), spec_.size(), is_sorted);` -- start comes from the previous chunk's end, end from the live `const MSSpectrum& spec_`, and nothing relates the two. Both Chunk members are `Size` (size_t, MSSpectrum.h:58-59), so an inversion is not detectable by sign. The consumer builds iterators from them unchecked: src/openms/source/KERNEL/MSSpectrum.cpp:421 `std::stable_sort(select_indices.begin() + chunks[i].start, select_indices.begin() + chunks[i].end, comparePos)` and MSSpectrum.cpp:433 `std::inplace_merge(select_indices.begin() + chunks[first].start, ... + chunks[mid].end, ... + chunks[last].end, comparePos)`.
verdicts.change: MSSpectrum.h:87-101: `add()` now hoists the start into a local and throws Exception::Precondition (OPENMS_PRETTY_FUNCTION, message carrying both sizes) when `spec_.size() < start`, so an inverted or past-the-end chunk can never be recorded; added a Doxygen block documenting the new @exception. The complementary defensive re-validation of the caller-supplied vector at the top of sortByPositionPresorted lives in MSSpectrum.cpp, which belongs to kernel-spectrum-a, and was not touched.
verdicts.regression_risk: Both in-tree users only append between add() calls, so the new precondition cannot fire for them: TheoreticalSpectrumGenerator.cpp:129 builds Chunks(spectrum) and only push_back/emplace_backs before its chunks.add() calls (:194-207, :649-983), and MSSpectrum_test.cpp:884-892 emplace_backs monotonically. Risk is limited to code that deliberately shrinks a spectrum mid-chunking, which was undefined behaviour before.

verdicts.claim: An empty but correctly named ion-mobility array makes isSortedByIM() vacuously true and sortByIonMobility() a silent no-op, because neither relates the IM array length to the peak count and checkDataArraySizes_ exempts empty arrays.
verdicts.evidence: The claim still holds, in a file this group does not own. containsIMData() (src/openms/source/KERNEL/MSSpectrum.cpp:820-825) delegates to getIonMobilityArray__ (:808), which matches float arrays by *name* only. isSortedByIM() (MSSpectrum.cpp:506-512) takes `getFloatDataArrays()[im_data_index]` and returns `std::is_sorted(im_data.begin(), im_data.end())` with no comparison against size(); sortByIonMobility() (MSSpectrum.cpp:383-395) short-circuits on the same `!std::is_sorted(...)` and only reaches checkDataArraySizes_ via sort(). checkDataArraySizes_ (MSSpectrum.cpp:20-37) deliberately exempts empty arrays: `if (!arrays[i].empty() && arrays[i].size() != peaks)`.
verdicts.change: Nothing changed: the fix is entirely inside src/openms/source/KERNEL/MSSpectrum.cpp, owned by kernel-spectrum-a. Exact edit requested: in MSSpectrum.cpp, in sortByIonMobility() immediately after line 388 (`const auto& im_data = getFloatDataArrays()[im_data_index];`) and in isSortedByIM() immediately after line 509 (the same `im_data` binding), insert the same guard -- `if (im_data.size() != size()) { throw Exception::Precondition(__FILE__, __LINE__, OPENMS_PRETTY_FUNCTION, "Ion mobility array size (" + StringUtils::toStr(im_data.size()) + ") does not match spectrum size (" + StringUtils::toStr(size()) + ")"); }` -- with a comment saying WHY (an IM array is recognised by name alone, so an absent or undecodable binary array leaves it empty and std::is_sorted then reports the spectrum sorted although no peak carries a mobility value). I deliberately left the header docs for sortByIonMobility (MSSpectrum.h:314-321) and isSortedByIM (:331-335) unchanged so they do not contradict whichever way that group resolves it; once the guard lands, `@throws Exception::Precondition if the ion-mobility array does not hold one value per peak` should be added to both.
verdicts.regression_risk: Adding the guard makes spectra whose IM array failed to decode throw where they previously reported 'sorted'; mzML readers that register a named-but-empty IM array would surface as errors rather than silently unsorted frames.

verdicts.claim: mergePeaks replaces the peak vector without updating or clearing the inherited RangeManager, so a chromatogram whose ranges were current afterwards reports a range that no longer contains its own points; select() documents the opposite, benign direction and mergePeaks documents nothing.
verdicts.evidence: The claim held. src/openms/source/KERNEL/MSChromatogram.cpp:557-562 assigned the merged vector (`ContainerType::assign(temp.begin(), new_end)`) and fell straight through to the add_meta block -- no clearRanges(), no updateRanges() -- while select() carries the explicit note at src/openms/include/OpenMS/KERNEL/MSChromatogram.h:439-440 ('Cached ranges are NOT recomputed ... selecting a subset can leave them too wide -- call updateRanges()'). The merge both extends RT (other's peaks) and raises intensities (summed at coincident RTs), so the cache can only end up too narrow.
verdicts.change: MSChromatogram.cpp:571-574: call updateRanges() at the end of the merge, with a comment saying why recomputation is preferred over leaving stale values that still look current (unlike select(), a merge can only lose data this way). MSChromatogram.h:477 adds the matching `@note The cached ranges are recomputed, since a merge can only widen them.`
verdicts.regression_risk: Ranges are now populated after a merge where they used to stay empty or stale. MSChromatogram::operator== (MSChromatogram.cpp:61-69) explicitly does not compare ranges, so MSChromatogram_test.cpp:1237-1254's TEST_EQUAL(a, c) is unaffected. In an OPENMS_ASSERTIONS build a merge that happens not to move the extrema now triggers updateRanges()'s (harmless, debug-only) 'already up-to-date' warning.

verdicts.claim: mergePeaks leaves float/string/integer data arrays at their pre-merge length, so the chromatogram fails its own checkDataArraySizes_ and the next sortByPosition/sortByIntensity/sort/select throws; the header @note understates this as 'not guaranteed to be correct'.
verdicts.evidence: The claim held. checkDataArraySizes_ (MSChromatogram.cpp:355-372) throws Exception::Precondition for any non-empty array whose size differs from the peak count, and it is called from select() via selectUnchecked() (MSChromatogram.cpp:375-390, :517) and from the sort() template; mergePeaks (MSChromatogram.cpp:557-562) grew the peak vector and never touched float_data_arrays_/string_data_arrays_/integer_data_arrays_. The old header text was MSChromatogram.h:472 ('Peak level metadata ... is not guaranteed to be correct after merging').
verdicts.change: MSChromatogram.cpp:565-569: clear the three peak-parallel arrays inside mergePeaks, with a comment saying why (they describe the pre-merge peaks and the size mismatch would make the chromatogram's own sort()/select() throw), mirroring clear() at MSChromatogram.cpp:343-346. MSChromatogram.h:472-475: the @note now states the arrays are dropped and why.
verdicts.regression_risk: Callers that merged and then read the destination's data arrays now see them empty instead of stale-and-mis-sized. The only in-tree caller (MSChromatogram_test.cpp:1237-1254) uses chromatograms without data arrays, and operator== compares the (now equally empty) arrays, so it is unaffected.

verdicts.claim: The merge helper setSumSimilarUnion is defined at global namespace scope with external linkage, so it is exported from libOpenMS and an equally named global function elsewhere is an undiagnosed ODR violation.
verdicts.evidence: The claim held: src/openms/source/KERNEL/MSChromatogram.cpp:17 is `using namespace OpenMS;` and the definition at :477 (pre-fix) was `OpenMS::MSChromatogram::Iterator setSumSimilarUnion(...)` outside any namespace, with no `static` and no anonymous namespace. Its only use is MSChromatogram::mergePeaks in the same translation unit (MSChromatogram.cpp:560).
verdicts.change: MSChromatogram.cpp:482: the definition is now `static`, with a comment saying why internal linkage is required (detail of mergePeaks in this TU; external linkage would export the symbol and make a same-named global elsewhere an undiagnosed ODR violation).
verdicts.regression_risk: None within the tree: the symbol has no declaration in any header and no other translation unit references it (grep for setSumSimilarUnion hits only MSChromatogram.cpp). Out-of-tree code linking against the previously exported symbol would now fail to link, which is the intended tightening.

verdicts.claim: mergePeaks takes a non-const MSChromatogram& and marks it [in,out] although the body only reads it, so a caller holding a const reference must copy the whole chromatogram.
verdicts.evidence: The claim held. Declaration at MSChromatogram.h:479 (pre-fix) `void mergePeaks(MSChromatogram& other, bool add_meta=false);` with `@param[in,out] other`; the body (MSChromatogram.cpp:557-565, pre-fix) only calls other.size(), other.begin(), other.end() and other.getMZ() -- the last being a const member (MSChromatogram.cpp:81-84) -- and writes nothing through the reference.
verdicts.change: MSChromatogram.h:484 and MSChromatogram.cpp:557: the parameter is now `const MSChromatogram& other` and the tag `@param[in] ... it is only read`. To make that possible, the helper's two input ranges became ConstIterator (MSChromatogram.cpp:482-485 and the smaller_RT lambda at :498); the output iterator stays mutable. No body logic changed.
verdicts.regression_risk: Binding a non-const lvalue to a const& is unchanged for existing callers, and the only caller is MSChromatogram_test.cpp:1250 (`a.mergePeaks(b, true)`), which still compiles. No header declares the helper and no pyOpenMS binding wraps mergePeaks (grep over the whole OpenMS4-tests tree finds only MSChromatogram.h, MSChromatogram.cpp and MSChromatogram_test.cpp). The test's START_SECTION text at MSChromatogram_test.cpp:1237 still spells the old signature -- cosmetic only, and that file is in no group's owned_files.

verdicts.evidence: The claim held verbatim: src/openms/source/METADATA/ChromatogramSettings.cpp:149-154 (pre-fix) was `std::ostream & operator<<(std::ostream & os, const ChromatogramSettings & /*spec*/)` printing only '-- CHROMATOGRAMSETTINGS BEGIN --' and '-- CHROMATOGRAMSETTINGS END --', and it is reached from MSChromatogram's stream operator at src/openms/source/KERNEL/MSChromatogram.cpp:19-24 via `os << static_cast<const ChromatogramSettings&>(chrom)`.
verdicts.change: ChromatogramSettings.cpp:149-168: the parameter is named (matching the header declaration's `spec`, ChromatogramSettings.h:153) and the block now prints native ID, the chromatogram type name via the house idiom `ChromatogramSettings::ChromatogramNames[static_cast<size_t>(...)]` (as FileInfo.cpp:1683 does), precursor m/z, product m/z and every meta value (getKeys/getMetaValue(...).toString()). The delimiters are kept deliberately, with a comment saying why, so text-matching consumers keep working.
verdicts.regression_risk: No reference document carries this text: grep for 'CHROMATOGRAMSETTINGS' over the package hits only this source file, and the three class tests that stream a chromatogram or experiment assert substrings only (MSChromatogram_test.cpp:1256-1273 checks 'MSCHROMATOGRAM BEGIN' and '47.11'; MSExperiment_test.cpp:1662-1666 likewise). SpectrumSettings.cpp:185-190 keeps the identical empty-block pattern -- same defect class, different file, not owned here -- so the two settings dumps now differ in verbosity.

verdicts.claim: The OPENMS_ASSERTIONS check in updateRanges reads an empty dimension as 0 both before and after, so the very first, necessary call on a chromatogram without a cached range logs 'ranges were already up-to-date'.
verdicts.evidence: The claim held. src/openms/source/KERNEL/MSChromatogram.cpp:523-527 (pre-fix) computed `rt_min = RangeRT::isEmpty() ? 0 : getMinRT()` (and the three siblings the same way), recomputed them identically after the rebuild (:543-546), and warned on numeric equality alone (:548-552). For `MSChromatogram c; c.updateRanges();` all eight values are 0, and so they are for a single peak at RT 0 with intensity 0, so the warning fired on a first call that was entirely necessary. The 0 substitution is needed because RangeBase::getMin/getMax throw Exception::InvalidRange on an empty range (RangeManager.h:128-145).
verdicts.change: MSChromatogram.cpp:525-528: capture `const bool had_ranges = !RangeRT::isEmpty() && !RangeIntensity::isEmpty();` before clearing, with a comment saying why the numeric comparison alone cannot tell 'no range yet' from 'range unchanged', and require it in the warning condition at :549.
verdicts.regression_risk: Debug-build diagnostics only; release builds compile the block out entirely. The check now stays silent for a first call and still fires for a genuinely redundant refresh of an already-populated range.

verdicts.claim: Non-const MRMFeature::getFeature/getPrecursorFeature use map::operator[], so an unknown key default-inserts key->0 and returns an unrelated feature.
verdicts.evidence: MRMFeature.cpp:82-85 was `return features_.at(feature_map_[key]);` and 125-128 was `return precursor_features_.at(precursor_feature_map_[key]);`. std::map::operator[] inserts {key,0} on a miss, so the call returned features_[0] and a later getFeatureIDs() listed the typo key. The const overloads (87-90, 130-133) used .at() and threw a bare std::out_of_range. The claim holds. Production callers (MRMFeatureFinderScoring.cpp:379-450, EmgScoring.h:67, MRMFeatureAccessOpenMS.cpp:221-266, MRMTransitionGroup.h subset) only ask for keys that exist. MRMTransitionGroupPicker.h:383 picks each chromatogram by transition nativeID and adds its sub-feature at :946 for every transition, and chromatogramIdsMatch() is required at :319. No code catches std::out_of_range around these lookups.
verdicts.change: Added a file-local helper, featureIndex_(map, key, OPENMS_PRETTY_FUNCTION), in MRMFeature.cpp. It looks the key up with find() and throws Exception::ElementNotFound naming the key. All four accessors, const and non-const, now use it, so a missing key never changes the map and fails the same way whatever the constness. Added #include <OpenMS/CONCEPT/Exception.h>.
verdicts.regression_risk: A lookup of a key that was never added now throws ElementNotFound. Before, the non-const overload returned the wrong feature and the const overload threw std::out_of_range. Every existing caller and class test (MRMFeature_test.cpp:94-104, 199-209; MRMTransitionGroupPicker_test.cpp) looks up keys that exist, so no expected output changes.

verdicts.claim: MRMFeature::addFeature/addPrecursorFeature append on a repeated key, leaving the earlier feature stored but unreachable.
verdicts.evidence: MRMFeature.cpp:70-80 and 105-115 did push_back and then `feature_map_[key] = Int(size)-1`. A second add under the same key moved the map entry to the new element and left the old one in features_ with no key pointing at it, so getFeatures().size() (2) and getFeatureIDs().size() (1) disagreed. The claim holds. This also matters downstream: MRMFeatureAccessOpenMS.cpp:259-265 requires getFeatures().size() to equal the transition lookup-id count and indexes features_ by position.
verdicts.change: On a repeated key, both overloads of each function now overwrite the feature at the index already stored, using map::emplace and assigning in place on a hit. Nothing is left stranded, and the vector stays aligned with the key map in insertion order. I did not copy addTransition's throw. MRMFeature has no hasFeature() for callers to check first. The picker keys features by chromatogram.getNativeID() (MRMTransitionGroupPicker.h:946, :1077), so a repeated nativeID in input data would abort a whole run instead of keeping the last-written value, which is what lookups already returned.
verdicts.regression_risk: Only calls that repeat a key behave differently: getFeatures().size() no longer grows. No class test adds a repeated key (MRMFeature_test.cpp:100-101, 140-141, 152-153, 189-190, 205-206 all use distinct keys), and the picker adds one key per transition.

verdicts.claim: MRMTransitionGroup::isInternallyConsistent is made only of OPENMS_PRECONDITIONs and so returns true in every release build.
verdicts.evidence: MRMTransitionGroup.h:291-297 held three OPENMS_PRECONDITIONs and then `return true;`. Macros.h:85-98 defines OPENMS_PRECONDITION as empty unless OPENMS_ASSERTIONS is set, and src/openms/CMakeLists.txt:27-31 sets that only for CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug. MRMFeatureFinderScoring.cpp:1440 relies on the result: `if (!trgroup_it->second.isInternallyConsistent()) throw Exception::IllegalArgument(...)`. That check could never fire in a release build. The claim holds. The empty release expansion in Macros.h is intentional and was not changed.
verdicts.change: The function now tests the transition and chromatogram counts, then the map sizes, then isMappingConsistent_(), and returns the result. I removed the OPENMS_PRECONDITIONs from this query. Otherwise a Debug build would throw Precondition where callers expect a bool. Callers that want to fail fast already wrap it in OPENMS_PRECONDITION (MRMTransitionGroupPicker.h:318, :565). Removed '(no runtime overhead in release mode)' from the doc comment, since it described the defect, and added a comment saying why the result is computed. Extended the isInternallyConsistent section in MRMTransitionGroup_test.cpp with two cases that must return false: a transition with no chromatogram, and equal counts with a mismatched key.
verdicts.regression_risk: In release builds the function now walks chromatogram_map_ once per call. Its only release-mode caller runs once per transition group at load time (MRMFeatureFinderScoring.cpp:1438). That caller builds groups by adding one transition and one chromatogram under the same key (:1430-1431), so the check cannot newly fire on that path. Debug builds that used to throw Precondition from this function now get false.

verdicts.claim: IDScoresAsMetaValue writes '<id>transition_names' twice, possibly in place of a score that is now missing.
verdicts.evidence: MRMFeature.cpp:142 and :152 both did `setMetaValue(id + "transition_names", idscores.ind_transition_names)`. A script compared the 42 members of OpenSwath_Ind_Scores (OpenSwathScores.h:180-231) with the idscores.<member> references: 43 calls, 42 distinct keys, and no member left out. So the second write is redundant, and the report's guess that a score is missing is wrong. A second setMetaValue on the same name reuses the same MetaInfo registry index, so removing it changes neither values nor key order. No file under src/tests/class_tests/openms/data/ contains id_target_transition_names. The class tests that read the key (MRMFeatureFinderScoring_test.cpp:284-285) still see it.
verdicts.change: Deleted the duplicate write at the former line 152.
verdicts.regression_risk: None. The same key and value are written once instead of twice.

verdicts.claim: getLibraryIntensity clamps negatives across the caller's whole vector, not just the entries it appended.
verdicts.evidence: MRMTransitionGroup.h:325 was `for (Size i = 0; i < result.size(); i++)`, running after values were appended to a vector the caller owns. So a -5.0 the caller had put in beforehand became 0.0. The claim holds. The only non-test caller is TransitionGroupOpenMS::getLibraryIntensities (MRMFeatureAccessOpenMS.h:192-195), and it is used only from class tests. Every existing call passes an empty vector.
verdicts.change: The function records result.size() before appending and clamps from that index, with a comment on why. Added a pre-filled-vector case to the getLibraryIntensity section of MRMTransitionGroup_test.cpp: -5.0 stays -5.0, and the appended values are 3 and 0.
verdicts.regression_risk: None for existing callers, which all pass empty vectors.

verdicts.claim: subset() re-keys precursor chromatograms by nativeID, so a valid group whose precursors share a nativeID (e.g. both empty) throws InvalidValue.
verdicts.evidence: MRMTransitionGroup.h:355-359 looped over precursor_chromatograms_ and called `addPrecursorChromatogram(pc, pc.getNativeID())`. addPrecursorChromatogram (:231-240) throws InvalidValue on a duplicate key. In MRMTransitionGroup_test.cpp the file-scope chrom1/chrom2 never get a nativeID (setNativeID is never called on them), yet they are stored under different keys (:204, :211). The claim holds. In the production pipeline precursors are always stored under their nativeID (OpenSwathWorkflow.cpp:1395), and precursor lookups use the nativeID (MRMTransitionGroupPicker.h:1197), so real data is unaffected.
verdicts.change: subset() now inverts precursor_chromatogram_map_ into a per-index key list (map values are storage indices by construction) and copies each precursor chromatogram in storage order under its original key. Storage order matters because the picker treats precursor index 0 as the monoisotopic trace (MRMTransitionGroupPicker.h:1056). A comment explains the reason. Extended the subset section of MRMTransitionGroup_test.cpp: two precursor chromatograms with unset nativeIDs under 'prec1'/'prec2' now survive subset() under those keys.
verdicts.regression_risk: Nothing changes when key == nativeID, which is every production construction path. Order is kept exactly, so nothing depending on index 0 moves. Only groups whose precursor keys differ from their nativeIDs behave differently: the copy keeps the stored key, which is what the copy should do.

verdicts.claim: subsetDependent calls chromatogram_map_.at() without the hasChromatogram guard that subset has, so a missing chromatogram escapes as a bare std::out_of_range.
verdicts.evidence: MRMTransitionGroup.h:397 was `addChromatogram(chromatograms_[chromatogram_map_.at(tr_it->getNativeID())], ...)` with no check, while subset guards at :348. The claim holds. The production caller, MRMFeatureFinderScoring.cpp:340-341 (splitTransitionGroupsIdentification_), works on groups built with one transition and one chromatogram per key (:1430-1431), so valid input never reaches the failure.
verdicts.change: subsetDependent now checks hasChromatogram before copying and throws Exception::ElementNotFound(__FILE__, __LINE__, OPENMS_PRETTY_FUNCTION, nativeID), with a comment on why. I chose a clear error over copying subset's silent skip. Skipping would build a group whose transitions and chromatograms disagree, and it would fail later with no context, e.g. in buildIdentificationSignalNoiseEstimators at MRMFeatureFinderScoring.cpp:664-672. The new check is covered in the rewritten subsetDependent test section (see CPP-104).
verdicts.regression_risk: Only the exception type changes, from std::out_of_range to Exception::ElementNotFound, on input that already failed. Valid groups behave the same.

verdicts.claim: The subsetDependent class-test section calls subset(), so subsetDependent itself is never tested.
verdicts.evidence: MRMTransitionGroup_test.cpp:328-352 opens START_SECTION(MRMTransitionGroup subsetDependent(...)) but calls `mrmtrgroupsub = mrmtrgroup.subset(transition_ids);` on a group with no chromatograms or features. The claim holds.
verdicts.change: Rewrote the section to call subsetDependent. The fixture now adds a chromatogram per transition, which subsetDependent needs, plus an MRMFeature with sub-features for both transitions. The original two-id assertions are kept unchanged (size 2, 3, 0), and subsetDependent gives exactly those values. Added a single-id case: 1 transition, 1 chromatogram, and the feature copied whole with both sub-feature IDs. Added TEST_EXCEPTION(Exception::ElementNotFound, ...) for a selected transition that has no chromatogram. No reference data or existing expected values were changed.

verdicts.claim: FeatureHandle::asMutable() const_casts away constness of a possibly const object; a non-const overload should replace the cast.
verdicts.evidence: src/openms/include/OpenMS/KERNEL/FeatureHandle.h:153-159 does the cast, and the class doc at :69-88 states its purpose: ConsensusFeature stores handles in a std::set, which exposes const_iterators only although the stored handles are not const objects. All six in-tree callers dereference such an iterator of a NON-const ConsensusFeature (MapAlignmentTransformer.cpp:167, MapAlignmentAlgorithmPoseClustering.cpp:81, ConsensusMapNormalizerAlgorithmMedian.cpp:134 and :149, ...Quantile.cpp:169, ...Threshold.cpp:103), so no genuinely const object is written and the const_cast is well defined there. The proposed non-const overload cannot replace it: those callers never hold a non-const iterator to begin with. What was actually wrong was the comment - line 151 read 'TODO use const_cast' while the code on the next line already used const_cast.
verdicts.change: Replaced the stale TODO with a comment saying why the cast exists (std::set hands out const iterators; the static_cast to FeatureHandleMutable_ is what hides the order-breaking mutators), FeatureHandle.h:155-157, and added an @note to the method doc (FeatureHandle.h:84-88) spelling out the precondition: only the access path may be const, writing through asMutable() on a genuinely const FeatureHandle is undefined behaviour. No signature changed.
verdicts.regression_risk: None - comment-only change, no code or signature touched.

verdicts.claim: FeatureHandle IndexLess section sets lhs.setUniqueId twice and never rhs; StandardTypes_test constructs PeakSpectrum/PeakMap twice and never Chromatogram; BinnedSpectrum constructor section title omits bool unit_ppm.
verdicts.evidence: Confirmed in all three files. FeatureHandle_test.cpp:187-190 (before the fix) read lhs.setMapIndex(2); lhs.setUniqueId(77); rhs.setMapIndex(4); lhs.setUniqueId(29); - rhs's unique id stayed 0 and the map indices differed, so the equal-map-index branch of IndexLess (FeatureHandle.h:160-169, 'if (left.map_index_ == right.map_index_) return left.getUniqueId() < right.getUniqueId();') was never exercised. verdicts.claim: The sortPeptideIdentifications comparator returns true whenever its left argument is empty, so two empty PeptideIdentifications compare true in both directions - no strict weak ordering, undefined behaviour in std::sort.

verdicts.claim: ConsensusFeature::Ratio has a user-provided empty default constructor and no member initialiser, so double ratio_value_ is indeterminate; the virtual destructor is pointless and costs a vtable pointer per ratio.

The laziness is kept (getConvexHulls() hands out a mutable vector, so there is no point at which eager computation would be correct) and no lock was added, because a std::mutex or std::once_flag member would make Feature non-copyable and non-movable - instead the data race is now documented at Feature.h:98-101: the cache write makes concurrent calls on one feature unsafe, fill the cache once up front (the idiom Feature_test.cpp:187 already uses).

verdicts.claim: RangeBase::setMin/setMax/extend accept NaN and infinity, breaking the rule that a range is either valid (min <= max) or empty (min > max).
verdicts.evidence: Before the change, RangeManager.h setMin (old 113-117) and setMax (old 120-124) had no check. With setMin(NaN), `max_ < NaN` is false, so the result is min_=NaN, max_=lowest(). Then isEmpty() (`min_ > max_`, line 90) and `min_ <= max_` are both false, and contains(x) is false for every x. A standalone mock compiled with clang++ printed 'isEmpty=0 valid=0 contains(0)=0'. The extend part of the claim is only half right. extend(double) (now 169-173) and extend(const RangeBase&) (now 159-163) use std::min/std::max, and those keep the current bound when the other value is NaN, so the rule still holds. The mock printed 'extend 1,NaN,3: [1,3]', and an empty range stays empty. extend runs once per peak in MSSpectrum::updateRanges (MSSpectrum.cpp:587-588) and in MSChromatogram, Mobilogram and FeatureMap, so adding a branch there is not justified. Checked every RangeBase setMin/setMax caller in all packages: MathFunctions.h:136-137 (inputs guarded by a min < max precondition), SwathMapMassCorrection.cpp:261/532 (value comes from map operator[], so it is finite), IonMobilityBinning.cpp:101-102 (only reached when `!cvs.empty()`, so splitByFAIMSCV's NaN placeholder at IMDataConverter.cpp:37 never gets there), PlotCanvas/Plot1DCanvas (literal 0), and the pyOpenMS pass-through bindings. No class test passes NaN or infinity to these setters. No range code uses infinity() anywhere.
verdicts.change: RangeManager.h setMin (112-122) and setMax (124-132) now throw Exception::InvalidRange with OPENMS_PRETTY_FUNCTION when given a NaN or infinite value (checked with std::isfinite, which needs <cmath>, already included at line 16). This matches the InvalidRange the two-argument constructor already throws. A comment explains why: a NaN bound leaves the range neither valid nor empty, and an infinite bound breaks center() and getSpan(). Added '@throws Exception::InvalidRange if ... is not finite' to both setters and to the 8 per-dimension wrappers (setMin/MaxRT, MZ, Intensity, Mobility), which already list getMin's throw. extend(double) and extend(const RangeBase&) keep their code but gained an @note: a NaN value leaves the range unchanged on purpose, because the function runs per peak and bad values in the data must not corrupt the range. The constructors RangeBase(double) and RangeBase(double,double) were left as they are, because the report does not name them and they are the 'I want exactly this range' path; see notes.
verdicts.regression_risk: Code that passes NaN or +-inf to setMin/setMax (or setMin<Dim>/setMax<Dim>, including through pyOpenMS) now gets an exception instead of a silently broken range. No such caller exists in core, topp, desktop or pyopenms, and no class test does it. Signatures and behaviour for finite values are unchanged. Nothing changes in the hot extend() path.

verdicts.claim: The notes on IsInCollisionEnergyRange, IsInIsolationWindowSizeRange and IsInIsolationWindow say MS1 spectra and spectra without a collision energy return true, but the code returns false, and reverse does not change that.

Both come before the `reverse_` branch, so reverse never inverts them. The old notes (517, 518, 570, 615) said 'return true'. The code is the intended behaviour: the inline comment 'leave non-fragmentation spectra untouched' means that with remove_if(), returning false keeps the spectrum. RangeUtils_test.cpp:372-398 only covers MS2 spectra, so nothing depends on the wrong wording.

The three @note blocks (now 517-519, 571-572, 617-618) say the predicate returns false for MS1 spectra (and, for IsInCollisionEnergyRange, for spectra without a collision energy), that @p reverse does not invert this early return, and that remove_if() therefore keeps those spectra. verdicts.claim: The DRange default constructor is documented as giving all-zero coordinates, but it actually produces the empty sentinel.
verdicts.evidence: DRange.h 74-77: `DRange() : Base() {}`. The DIntervalBase default constructor (DIntervalBase.h 55-59) sets min_ to PositionType::maxPositive() and max_ to PositionType::minNegative(), which are numeric_limits max() and lowest() (DPosition.h:332-341). That is exactly DIntervalBase::empty (DIntervalBase.h 369-371), so isEmpty() is true. The old doc at DRange.h:72 said 'Creates a range with all coordinates zero.' An all-zero range is the separate static DIntervalBase::zero (DIntervalBase.h:366).
verdicts.change: Rewrote the constructor doc (DRange.h 69-75). It now says the constructor creates an empty range (the base-class sentinel: every minimum is the largest representable value and every maximum the smallest, so isEmpty() is true) and points to DRange<D>::zero for an all-zero range. The code is unchanged.
verdicts.regression_risk: None, only comments changed.

verdicts.claim: DRange::united of two empty ranges returns the range covering everything instead of an empty range.
verdicts.evidence: DRange.h united() (old 178-195): for two empty operands, united_min[i] = min(DBL_MAX, DBL_MAX) = DBL_MAX and united_max[i] = max(-DBL_MAX, -DBL_MAX) = -DBL_MAX. setMinMax() then calls normalize_() (DIntervalBase.h 342-351), which swaps these inverted corners into [-DBL_MAX, +DBL_MAX]. A clang++ mock of the template hierarchy printed 'united(empty,empty).isEmpty()=0 min0=-1.79769e+308 max0=1.79769e+308'. When only one operand is empty the result is already correct, because the non-empty operand sets both bounds. The existing tests (DRange_test.cpp:362-376) only unite non-empty ranges.
verdicts.change: DRange.h:185 adds `if (this->isEmpty() && other_range.isEmpty()) return DRange<D>::empty;` before the corner computation. The comment says why: without it, setMinMax() would swap the two inverted sentinel corners back into order and return the universal range. Also added an @note to the doc. `this->` is needed because DIntervalBase<D> is a dependent base. `DRange<D>::empty` converts through the existing DRange(const Base&) constructor, as line 182 already does. The mock compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra and, after the change, prints isEmpty()=1 for empty+empty while the empty+[a] and [a]+[b] results stay the same.
verdicts.regression_risk: Only the case where both operands are fully empty changes: it now returns empty instead of [-DBL_MAX, DBL_MAX]. Every other input gives the same result as before. No caller of united() exists outside DRange_test.cpp. Not changed: a range that is empty in only some dimensions (reachable via setDimMinMax/assign) still widens to the universal range in those dimensions; see notes.

verdicts.claim: The @param doc of DRange::extend(PositionType) says invalid min/max are not fixed, but the code collapses an inverted dimension to its centre.
verdicts.evidence: DRange.h:329 (old 321): `if (min_[i] > max_[i]) min_[i] = max_[i] = (min_[i] + max_[i]) / 2;`. The same doc block already says 'may result in min==max (but never min>max)' (old 305). The old @param at line 310 said 'Resulting invalid min/max are not fixed automatically!', which contradicts both. DRange_test.cpp:427-432 ('test shrinking to a single point') asserts the collapse (min=max=1.0 after extend({-200,0})), so the comment was stale, not the code.
verdicts.change: Rewrote the @param text (DRange.h 317-318): a dimension that would become inverted (min > max) is collapsed to its centre point, so min <= max always holds afterwards. The code is unchanged.
verdicts.regression_risk: None, only comments changed.

verdicts.claim: The DIntervalBase default constructor is documented as putting the corners at infinity, but it uses the finite numeric_limits extremes.
verdicts.evidence: DIntervalBase.h 55-59: `min_(PositionType::maxPositive()), max_(PositionType::minNegative())`. DPosition.h:332-341 defines these as `std::numeric_limits<CoordinateType>::lowest()` and `(std::numeric_limits<CoordinateType>::max)()`, both finite. The old doc at line 51 said 'Creates an empty interval with corners at infinity.', so a std::isinf test on the corners never matches.
verdicts.change: Rewrote the constructor doc (DIntervalBase.h 48-54). It now says the constructor creates an empty interval with minPosition() = PositionType::maxPositive() and maxPosition() = PositionType::minNegative(), that these are the finite numeric_limits max() and lowest() rather than infinity, and that testing the corners for infinity never matches. The code is unchanged.
verdicts.regression_risk: None, only comments changed.

verdicts.claim: With strip_namespaces=true, plain path segments raise a parse error, and '@p:attr' loses its '@' attribute marker.
verdicts.evidence: StringUtils.h:596-609: split() puts the whole string in the vector and returns false when there is no delimiter, so the vector has one element, not zero. CVMappingFile.cpp (before the edit) lines 83-98 split each segment on ':' and expected an empty vector for 'no prefix'. Since empty segments are already skipped at line 78, 'mzML' produced size 1 and reached fatalError at line 97. For '@p:accession', line 93 kept only split[1], so the '@' was dropped. verdicts.claim: A CVMappingFile load that throws leaves references, rules and a partial rule behind, and they leak into the next load.

verdicts.claim: m.setCVReferences(m.getCVReferences()) appends to the vector while iterating over it, which is undefined behaviour.
verdicts.evidence: CVMappings.cpp:68-75 (before the edit) iterated the const-reference argument while calling push_back on cv_references_vector_. getCVReferences() (lines 77-80) returns a reference to that same member, so a reallocation invalidates the loop iterators.

verdicts.claim: Unknown requirementLevel or cvTermsCombinationLogic values silently fall back to MUST or OR.

So 'MAYY' became MUST (a stricter rule) and 'ANDD' became OR (a looser one). Every shipped and test mapping file uses only valid values: share/OpenMS/MAPPING and class_tests/openms/data contain requirementLevel MAY x90, MUST x69, SHOULD x2 and logic OR x106, AND x51, XOR x2.

verdicts.claim: The compression sniffing in XMLFile::parse_ builds a string from uninitialized bytes when the file is shorter than 2 bytes.
verdicts.evidence: XMLFile.cpp (before the edit) lines 145-148: 'char tmp_bz[3];' was not initialized, the result of read(tmp_bz, 2) was not checked, and only tmp_bz[2] was set before std::string(tmp_bz). An empty file leaves bytes 0 and 1 indeterminate, and a 1-byte file leaves byte 1 indeterminate. Line 160 then also reads bz[1] on a string that can be shorter than 2.

verdicts.claim: The descendant-unit fallback in SemanticValidator compares allowed-unit descendants with the measured term, not with the supplied unit.

verdicts.change: The lambda now compares with parsed_term.unit_accession (SemanticValidator.cpp:405), with a comment. The unused local was removed.

verdicts.claim: Unmapped locateTerm lookups throw before any validation but return false afterwards, because the callbacks insert empty rule lists.
verdicts.evidence: The throwing half is already gone: locateTerm now uses rules_.find() and returns false for an unmapped path (SemanticValidator.cpp:622-626 after the edit, 538-542 before), so its answer no longer depends on history. The mechanism was still present: onEndElement (before the edit, line 147) and handleTerm_ (line 277) used rules_[path], adding an empty vector for every distinct element path of every validated file. That grew the mapping index, which should be read-only, across documents.

verdicts.claim: PeptideEvidence::hasValidLimits rejects 0..0 and accepts reversed or negative limits.
verdicts.evidence: PeptideEvidence.cpp:79-85 (before the edit) returned !(start==-1 || end==-1 || end==0). A single-residue N-terminal peptide (0..0) was rejected, while 5..2 and -7..3 were accepted. The header (PeptideEvidence.h:79-89) documents zero-based positions where end is the 'position of the last AA', i.e. inclusive, and producers follow that (PeptideIndexing.cpp:668 uses start+len-1). The only caller is IDFilter.h:451 (DigestionFilter). No test asserts hasValidLimits.
verdicts.change: hasValidLimits now returns start >= 0 && end >= 0 && start <= end (PeptideEvidence.cpp:86), with a comment explaining the inclusive contract and why end == N_TERMINAL_POSITION is a valid endpoint.
verdicts.regression_risk: Only IDFilter::DigestionFilter is affected. Reversed or negative evidences are now kept with a warning instead of being passed to isValidProduct with a negative length. 0..0 evidences are now checked instead of skipped. But IDFilter.h:459 passes length = end - start, one short for inclusive ends, so a 0..0 evidence gets length 0, isValidProduct_ returns false with a warning (EnzymaticDigestion.cpp:231), and that evidence is now filtered out. That off-by-one is in IDFilter.h, which this group does not own (see notes).

verdicts.claim: The xsd:date check uses DateTime::set(), so the plain date '2001-02-03' is rejected and date-time values are accepted.
verdicts.evidence: SemanticValidator.cpp (before the edit) lines 502-513 call DateTime::set(value). In DateTime.cpp:208-340, a string with '-' but no T/Z/+ goes to the 'yyyy-MM-dd hh:mm:ss' branch, which needs 6 fields (line ~287), and the protXML fallback also fails, so '2001-02-03' throws ParseError and is reported as an error. The PSI-MS CV types MS:1000747 (completion time), MS:1001017 and MS:1002435 as xsd:date, and MzMLHandler.cpp:3972 writes completion time as 'yyyy-MM-dd+hh:mm'. All 126 such values in 56 reference data files have that shape (e.g. '2025-12-29+18:07' in MzMLFile_4_indexed.mzML). As an xsd:date, the +18:07 part would be an invalid timezone, so strict checking would flag files that OpenMS itself writes.
verdicts.change: Added a file-local isXSDDate_() (SemanticValidator.cpp:26-74). It checks the W3C lexical form (4 or more year digits, 2-digit month and day, optional Z or ±hh:mm with hh<=14) and uses DateTime::setDate() for the calendar check. The XSD_DATE branch (lines 573-597) accepts a value if isXSDDate_ passes or, as before, DateTime::set parses it. Comments cite the spec and explain why date-time values stay accepted. The proposed rejection of timestamps was deliberately not applied.
verdicts.regression_risk: The check only accepts more values, so nothing previously accepted is now rejected. Plain or zoned dates that used to produce a 'should be xsd:date' error no longer do. No reference file validated in tests has a plain date, SemanticValidator_cv.obo has no xsd:date term, and no test expects this message. Negative years are still rejected, because DateTime's calendar starts at year 1.

verdicts.claim: .ibd array readers size the output from the declared IMS:1000103 count without checking offset + count*width against the .ibd length, so a hostile count commits up to 800 MB / 1.2 GB before fread comes up short.
verdicts.evidence: Pre-edit ImzMLHandlerHelper.cpp:39-51 validateCount_ only compares count against MAX_IBD_ARRAY_ELEMENTS (1e8); readMzArray then seeks (:132) and does out.resize(count) (:134) and, for FLOAT32, std::vector<float> tmp(count) (:140) before fread (:141). readFloatVector_ does the same at :209-213/:226. Nothing anywhere compares against the file length. Both reference fixtures end exactly at EOF (ImzMLFile_1_Example_Continuous: max offset+bytes 335976 = file size 335976; ImzMLFile_2_Example_Processed: 604744 = 604744, checked by parsing all 18 external arrays of each), so the check cannot reject them. The aux-length test (ImzMLFile_test.cpp:1448 sets length 999999) is filtered by the aux.count != peaks guard before readAuxArray on both paths (ImzMLHandler.cpp aux loop, OnDiscImzMLExperiment.cpp:127).
verdicts.change: Added elementWidth_() and validateRange_() in ImzMLHandlerHelper.cpp's anonymous namespace and called validateRange_ right after validateCount_ in readMzArray and readFloatVector_, i.e. before any resize or staging allocation. It throws ParseError for an unknown data type (same message the switch default produced, now before the allocation), for offset + bytes overflowing uint64, and for a range that ends past File::fileSize(ibd_path) (the existing SYSTEM/File helper; a stat, so the handle's position and stdio buffer are untouched). If the path cannot be stat'ed (fileSize returns -1), the check is skipped and the existing short-read check stays in charge. Updated the @throws and ibd_path @param docs in ImzMLHandlerHelper.h to say the path must be the one the handle was opened from (true for all three in-tree callers: ImzMLHandler uses meta_.ibd_file_path set from the path passed to openIBD, OnDiscImzMLExperiment uses ibd_path_ passed to fopen).
verdicts.regression_risk: A dataset whose declared ranges run past the .ibd now fails with 'declared range ... extends past the .ibd length' before allocating, where it used to fail with 'failed to read ...' after. The exception type (ParseError) is unchanged. Each array read adds a stat (two, because File::fileSize calls exists()). If a future caller passed a decorative ibd_path naming a different, shorter existing file, it would be falsely rejected; the header doc now forbids that.

verdicts.claim: ImzMLMeta::mz_data_type/int_data_type are only assigned inside the consumer's decode branch, so an index-only load (loadSpectraIndex, decode_ibd=false) returns them empty.
verdicts.evidence: Pre-edit ImzMLHandler.cpp:248-252 assigned the fields inside `if (handler_.ibd_ && handler_.decode_ibd_ && (ims->mz_meta.is_ext || ims->int_meta.is_ext))` (:198). ImzMLFile.cpp loadImpl_ calls connectDecodeConsumer(consumer, append_to_map, !index_only) (:563), and loadSpectraIndex passes index_only=true (:487), so decode_ibd_ is false. verdicts.change: Moved dtStr_ out of ImzMLInterceptConsumer into the file's anonymous namespace. The first non-UNKNOWN mz/int dt is now recorded in ImzMLHandler::onEndElement("spectrum"), inside the existing !skip_spectrum_ snapshot block, from cur_mz_meta_/cur_int_meta_. The decode-branch assignment is removed as redundant. A WHY comment is at the new site, and the ImzMLMeta section comment in ImzMLHandlerHelper.h now says the fields come from the first spectrum that declares a type and are filled by index-only parses too.
verdicts.regression_risk: Index-only loads (OnDiscImzMLExperiment::open) now report 'float32' etc. instead of ''. Existing expectations (ImzMLFile_test.cpp:588-589, 617-618) are 'float32' on the in-memory path and are unchanged, and checkMatchesIndexMeta_ does not compare these fields. Two corner cases change: a first spectrum with an untyped array no longer pins the summary to the literal 'unknown', and a file with only inline arrays now also gets the imzml:mz_data_type/int_data_type MetaValues.

verdicts.claim: An external aux array without MS:1000786 / MS:1000513-child identity is warned about only during in-memory decode and silently omitted from ImzMLSpectrumIndex::aux, so on-disc/index-only consumers cannot see it was dropped.
verdicts.evidence: Pre-edit ImzMLHandler.cpp:264-269: the warning sits in the aux-fill loop guarded by `handler_.ibd_ && handler_.decode_ibd_` (:258), so it never fires for loadSpectraIndex. :376-379: the index-build loop, which runs for every load, does a bare `continue`, and ImzMLSpectrumIndex (ImzMLHandlerHelper.h:102-139) had no field recording the drop.

verdicts.claim: verifyIbdUuid_ has two contradictory comment blocks; the first says a UUID mismatch is rejected, the code only warns.

The body (:88-123) only emits OPENMS_LOG_WARN and returns on every branch: missing/invalid UUID :91-96, unopenable .ibd :99-104, short header :108-114, mismatch :115-122.

verdicts.claim: IMS:1000091 SHA-1 and IMS:1000090 MD5 are parsed and mirrored as MetaValues but no read path ever verifies them.
verdicts.evidence: ImzMLHandler.cpp:703-704 (pre-edit numbering) store the values into meta_.ibd_sha1/ibd_md5, and ImzMLFile.cpp attachImzMLMeta_ (:152-159) mirrors them. No ImzML* source computes a digest; the only load-time integrity check is the 16-byte UUID compare in verifyIbdUuid_. An existing whole-file SHA-1 helper is available: FileHandler::computeFileHash (FileHandler.h:411, FileHandler.cpp:768). The declared digests are over the whole .ibd: `shasum` of ImzMLFile_2_Example_Processed.ibd gives 7e8fdb93053915d3edb51b70aa0619ac209964df and `md5` of ImzMLFile_1_Example_Continuous.ibd gives 4b5dd9fa84fafc955cfdd301f9ed55d7, matching the values the tests expect (ImzMLFile_test.cpp:586, 608).
verdicts.change: The reachable opt-in verification needs a new public declaration in ImzMLFile.h (or a PeakFileOptions flag), and this group owns neither file, so it is recorded in needs_shared_file. In an owned file, I rewrote the ImzMLMeta::ibd_sha1/ibd_md5 docs in ImzMLHandlerHelper.h to say they are the declared values, that no read path recomputes them, and that only the UUID header is (advisorily) checked. The documented contract now matches the behaviour until the API lands.
verdicts.regression_risk: None from the doc change. The proposed API is additive and opt-in, so it changes no existing load path or reference output.

verdicts.claim: OnDiscImzMLExperiment::open re-derives the .ibd path inline in an `if (ibd_path_.empty())` branch that can never be taken, duplicating ImzMLFile::inferIbdPath_.
verdicts.evidence: Pre-edit OnDiscImzMLExperiment.cpp:238-246. open() first calls loadSpectraIndex(imzml_path, meta_, index_, ibd_path_override) (:232), which goes to loadImpl_. loadImpl_ computes `ibd_path = override.empty() ? inferIbdPath_(filename) : override` (ImzMLFile.cpp:568), opens it (:569, which throws FileNotFound on failure), assigns handler.getImzMLMeta().ibd_file_path = ibd_path unconditionally (:570), and copies the meta out (:620). Nothing in handleIMSCvParam_ touches ibd_file_path. inferIbdPath_ (:633-643) returns a non-empty string for any input (at least ".ibd"). So meta_.ibd_file_path is never empty and already equals the override when one is given.
verdicts.change: Replaced the ternary and the dead block with `pimpl_->ibd_path_ = pimpl_->meta_.ibd_file_path;` plus a comment explaining that loadSpectraIndex resolves and records the path before parsing, so a second derivation could only drift.
verdicts.regression_risk: None. The override case yields the same string (meta_.ibd_file_path == override), and the removed branch was unreachable. The explicit override test (ImzMLFile_test.cpp:476) still opens the override path.

verdicts.claim: IonImage allocates width*height doubles plus a mask from file-supplied imzML dimensions with no ceiling, so a hostile header requests e.g. 80 GB.
verdicts.evidence: Pre-edit IonImage.cpp:21-28: resize() does intensities_.assign(width*height) and mask_.assign(width*height) with no bound. IonImageExtraction.h:89 constructs IonImage(geom.getWidth(), geom.getHeight()). MSImagingGeometry::setDimensions (MSImagingGeometry.cpp:16-20, not owned) stores the values unchecked, and ImzMLFile::buildImagingGeometry (ImzMLFile.cpp:382-386, 468-471) feeds it meta.max_count_x/y from IMS:1000042/1000043 or the largest coordinate.
verdicts.change: IonImage::resize (and therefore the (w,h) constructor and Internal::extractIonImage for both in-memory and on-disc) now throws Exception::InvalidValue when width*height exceeds a file-local MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = 16,777,216 (4096x4096, about 136 MB). The check runs before width_/height_ are touched, so a failed resize leaves the image unchanged. The comment explains that the dimensions come from the file being read. The value matches the Rust port's ceiling, so both implementations refuse the same inputs.
verdicts.regression_risk: extractIonImage on a genuine dataset whose grid exceeds 16.7 M pixels now throws InvalidValue instead of allocating. All in-tree tests use grids of at most a few pixels (IonImage_test.cpp:47-68, MSImagingExperiment_test, ImzMLFile_test 3x3 fixtures). IonImage.h (not owned) does not yet list the new @throws.

verdicts.claim: MSImagingRegion::fromMask computes max_x_/max_y_ as origin + extent - 1 in UInt, which wraps for origins near UINT_MAX and yields an inert inverted box instead of an error.
verdicts.evidence: Pre-edit MSImagingRegion.cpp:52-53 `reg.max_x_ = origin_x + width - 1; reg.max_y_ = origin_y + height - 1;`. The only prior checks are width/height != 0 (:37) and mask.size() == width*height (:42), and neither bounds the origin. For example, origin_x = 4294967295 with width 2 gives max_x_ = 0 < min_x_. contains() (:99) then returns false everywhere and getBBoxWidth() (:83) underflows. rectangle() (:17) rejects exactly this inverted state with InvalidValue.
verdicts.change: After the mask check, fromMask throws Exception::InvalidValue ("mask extends past the coordinate range") if origin_x > UINT_MAX - (width-1) or origin_y > UINT_MAX - (height-1). width and height are already known to be >= 1, so the subtraction cannot wrap. Added #include <limits> and a WHY comment tying the check to rectangle()'s invariant.
verdicts.regression_risk: Only inputs that previously produced a silently inert region now throw. The existing fromMask tests (MSImagingRegion_test.cpp:84-95, origin 10,20) are far from the limit.

verdicts.claim: SpectrumSettings::operator== (and so MSSpectrum::operator==) ignores im_type_ and im_peak_type_.
verdicts.evidence: At HEAD, SpectrumSettings.cpp:23-39 compares MetaInfoInterface, type_, native_id_, comment_, instrument_settings_, acquisition_info_, source_file_, precursors_, products_ and data_processing_, but not im_type_ or im_peak_type_ (declared at SpectrumSettings.h:170-171 and settable through setIMFormat/setIMPeakType, SpectrumSettings.cpp:80-97). MSSpectrum::operator== (MSSpectrum.cpp ~554) delegates to it and does not compare them either. The header documents plain equality, and its std::hash says it covers 'all fields used in operator=='.
verdicts.change: SpectrumSettings.cpp operator== now also compares im_type_ and im_peak_type_. A comment explains that the IM representation is part of the value. SpectrumSettings.h std::hash<SpectrumSettings> now hashes both enums, and its field list names them, so hash and equality still agree. operator!= stays the negation. MSSpectrum::operator== needed no change because it delegates.
verdicts.regression_risk: Two comparisons can now come out false where they were true: a spectrum whose IM peak type a loader filled in, compared against one where nothing set it. MzMLHandler.cpp:256 defaults any spectrum with IM data to IM_PROFILE. I checked the in-tree equality tests. MzMLFile_test.cpp:992-1063 round-trips load, store and load again, and the writer emits MS:1003441 (MzMLHandler.cpp:5324), so both sides agree. The MSSpectrum_test.cpp:322/337/363 snapshots are copies. PeakPickerIM, IMDataConverter and ImzML tests do no whole-spectrum ==. SpectrumSettings hash values change, but no test hard-codes one (SpectrumSettings_test.cpp:435ff only compares hashes with each other).

verdicts.claim: makePeakPositionUnique swaps in a default-constructed container, losing RT, MS level, native ID, precursors and metadata; the warning mentions only data arrays.
verdicts.evidence: At HEAD, SpectrumHelper.h:158 declares `PeakContainerT p_new;` (default constructed). Only merged peaks are pushed into it, then `std::swap(p_new, p)` at :196 replaces the whole record. The warning at :150 mentions only data arrays. The template is used with both MSSpectrum and MSChromatogram (SpectrumHelper_test.cpp:257-354; FeatureFinderMultiplexAlgorithm.cpp:480).
verdicts.change: p_new now starts as a copy of p followed by `p_new.clear(false)`. For both MSSpectrum (MSSpectrum.cpp:206-213) and MSChromatogram (MSChromatogram.cpp:335-346), clear(false) drops peaks, data arrays and cached ranges but keeps all descriptive metadata. So the only loss left is the one the warning announces, and data arrays and ranges end up exactly as before. A comment explains why the copy is made, and a @note in the Doxygen block states the contract (data arrays dropped, everything else kept). I used clear(false) because copySpectrumMeta is MSSpectrum-only and would not compile for chromatograms.
verdicts.regression_risk: Anyone who relied on the call wiping metadata now keeps it. The only in-tree caller, FeatureFinderMultiplexAlgorithm.cpp:480, builds a local chromatogram with no metadata, so nothing changes there. The existing SpectrumHelper_test only checks intensities and sizes. There is one extra O(n) copy of the peak vector, and it also pre-sizes p_new's capacity.

verdicts.claim: SpectrumRangeManager::byMSLevel defaults ms_level to 0, but level 0 is never stored per level, so the default call can only throw.
verdicts.evidence: At HEAD, SpectrumRangeManager.h:94 declares `byMSLevel(UInt ms_level = 0)` and looks the level up only in ms_level_ranges_. extend, extendRT, extendMZ and extendUnsafe (:84, :126, :137, :148) all send ms_level == 0 to the BaseType subobject and never insert key 0. So `byMSLevel()` always throws InvalidValue. SpectrumRangeManager_test.cpp:108-112 deliberately asserts that byMSLevel(0) throws. That test belongs to another group, so making level 0 return the base would break it; removing the trap default does not.
verdicts.change: Removed the default argument (`byMSLevel(UInt ms_level)`). The runtime behaviour, including the throw the class test asserts, is unchanged. The Doxygen now says level 0 never has an entry, that global ranges live in the BaseType subobject (use the manager directly, e.g. getMinRT()), and why the level is mandatory.
verdicts.regression_risk: External code that calls byMSLevel() with no argument no longer compiles. That call could only throw. No in-tree caller omits the argument: FileInfo.cpp, MultiplexClustering.cpp, FeatureFinderAlgorithmPicked.cpp, MSExperiment_test and SpectrumRangeManager_test all pass one, and the pyOpenMS binding (bind_kernel.cpp:3205) passes ms_level explicitly. The START_SECTION label at SpectrumRangeManager_test.cpp:102 still reads `= 0`, which is cosmetic only.

verdicts.claim: rasterizeIMFrame zero-fills the caller's buffer before the IM-array/peak-count check that can throw.
verdicts.evidence: At HEAD, MSSpectrum.cpp:895-898 computes total_pixels and runs std::fill, :901 returns early for an empty spectrum, and only then does :907 throw Precondition when im_data.size() != size(). A rejected call has already cleared the image.
verdicts.change: The size check now sits directly after getIMData(), before any write, guarded by `!this->empty()` so an empty spectrum still just zero-fills and returns, as MSSpectrum_rasterizeIMFrame_test.cpp:101-123 expects. The new overflow and range checks (CPP-077/078) are also placed before the fill, so every throw now happens before the buffer is touched. A comment explains why.
verdicts.regression_risk: None expected. The same exception is thrown under the same conditions; only the buffer is no longer cleared first. Empty-spectrum behaviour is unchanged.

verdicts.claim: im_bins * mz_bins is unchecked, so a wrapped product lets the per-peak write run past the caller's buffer.
verdicts.evidence: At HEAD, MSSpectrum.cpp:895 computes `const Size total_pixels = im_bins * mz_bins;` with no overflow check, and :951 computes `pixel_idx = mz_bin * im_bins + im_bin` from the unwrapped counts. Only zero counts are rejected (:875-884).
verdicts.change: Before any write, the call now throws Exception::InvalidValue (with OPENMS_PRETTY_FUNCTION) when `im_bins > numeric_limits<Size>::max() / sizeof(float) / mz_bins`. mz_bins != 0 is already guaranteed. Dividing by sizeof(float) also keeps `output + total_pixels` from overflowing. It holds both bin counts below 2^62, so the later `static_cast<Int64>(im_bins) - 1` clamp bounds and the bin casts stay well defined. Added `<limits>`.
verdicts.regression_risk: Only bin counts whose float buffer could not be addressed are rejected, so no real caller is affected.

verdicts.claim: NaN m/z or IM values pass the range filter and reach static_cast<Int64>, which is undefined behaviour and can give a negative index.
verdicts.evidence: At HEAD, MSSpectrum.cpp:931 filters with `mz < min_mz || mz > max_mz || im < min_im || im > max_im`, and every one of those is false for NaN. :937-938 then cast `(mz - min_mz) * mz_scale` to Int64, and :941-948 clamp only from above. The same UB is reachable through the bounds: `min_mz = -inf` passes the `min_mz >= max_mz` check (:890-897), gives mz_scale = 0, and `inf * 0` is NaN.
verdicts.change: Peaks with a non-finite m/z or IM value are now skipped before the range filter (std::isfinite). Before the buffer is touched, the call throws Exception::InvalidRange when either range or scale is not finite (infinite or NaN bounds, or a range so narrow that bins/range overflows). With finite bounds and scale, the scaled coordinate is finite and non-negative. The existing upper clamps now also have lower clamps, so the index stays inside the buffer whatever the cast produced. Added `<cmath>`. Comments explain each guard.
verdicts.regression_risk: Peaks with NaN or inf coordinates no longer land in an arbitrary pixel. Infinite bounds, which were UB, now throw InvalidRange. So do bounds like ±DBL_MAX whose difference overflows; those used to put every peak in bin 0. Finite, normal inputs render exactly as before.

verdicts.claim: sortByPositionPresorted treats a chunk list that does not cover the spectrum differently in its two branches and can leave peaks unsorted.
verdicts.evidence: At HEAD, MSSpectrum.cpp:401 returns early for a single chunk marked sorted, even if that chunk covers only part of the peaks. With no data arrays (:405-408) it ignores chunks and stable-sorts everything. With data arrays (:409-440) it sorts and merges only [chunks.front().start, chunks.back().end) and applies that permutation, so peaks outside the span stay put. Nothing checks the list. Its only producer, Chunks::add (MSSpectrum.h), always starts at the previous end. The only production caller is TheoreticalSpectrumGenerator.cpp:222, where every peak-appending block ends in chunks.add() (lines 194, 200, 207, 649, 681, 815-983), so real lists already tile [0, size()), and so does the class test at MSSpectrum_test.cpp:876-907.
verdicts.change: A non-empty chunk list is now checked up front. It must start at 0, end at size(), have no reversed chunk, and each chunk must start where the previous one ended. Otherwise Exception::Precondition (with OPENMS_PRETTY_FUNCTION) is thrown and nothing is mutated. With the list guaranteed to tile the spectrum, the plain stable_sort branch and the chunk-merge branch produce the same stable order; a comment on the plain branch says so. The single-chunk early return now also requires isSorted() (see CPP-080). An empty chunk list still returns immediately.
verdicts.regression_risk: A caller passing a list that does not tile the spectrum now gets an exception instead of a half-sorted spectrum. I found no such caller in core or the other packages (grep for sortByPositionPresorted finds only TheoreticalSpectrumGenerator and MSSpectrum_test). The added cost is O(number of chunks).

verdicts.claim: Chunks marked is_sorted are never checked, so std::inplace_merge can receive an unsorted range and silently produce a wrong order.
verdicts.evidence: At HEAD, MSSpectrum.cpp:419 sorts only chunks with `!chunks[i].is_sorted`. :433 then calls std::inplace_merge on all chunks, and that requires sorted inputs. The single-chunk early return at :401 trusts the flag as well. No later check catches it, because the data arrays are permuted consistently.
verdicts.change: In the merge branch, a chunk marked sorted is now checked with std::is_sorted using the same comparator, and stable-sorted if the claim is false, so inplace_merge always gets sorted inputs. The check short-circuits, so unsorted chunks are not scanned twice. The single-chunk early return now happens only if isSorted() confirms the claim; otherwise it falls through to the real sort. I chose to repair rather than throw because a wrong flag is a performance hint gone stale, and the function's job is to return a sorted spectrum. The cost is one linear scan, cheaper than the merge. Comments explain why.
verdicts.regression_risk: Output changes only when a chunk's is_sorted flag is wrong; the result then becomes correctly sorted instead of unspecified. TheoreticalSpectrumGenerator's flags appear correct for normal settings (ascending b/y ladders, ascending isotope clusters). A reference output could only move if it captured a spectrum where a flag was false, for example isotope clusters with an unusually large max_isotope overlapping the next prefix. There is one extra linear comparison scan per sort call, which matters a little in database search.

verdicts.claim: MSExperiment::updateRanges creates no per-level range entry for MS level 0, so SpectrumRangeManager::getMSLevels() omits 0 while MSExperiment::getMSLevels() reports it.
verdicts.evidence: MSExperiment.cpp:695-699 (before edit) calls extendUnsafe(*it)/extendRT(rt) and then extendUnsafe(*it, level)/extendRT(rt, level). SpectrumRangeManager.h:84,131,142,153 all do `ms_level == 0 ? BaseType::extend...(...) : ms_level_ranges_[ms_level]...`, so level 0 is deliberately the key for the global ranges. The second extend with the same values changes nothing. The SpectrumRangeManager.h doc (lines 90-93, updated by the CPP-062 group) already says level 0 never gets an entry. MSExperiment::getMSLevels (MSExperiment.cpp:753-764) collects every spectrum's level, 0 included. verdicts.claim: The left-boundary spread guard `static_cast<int>(idx - j - 1) >= 0` depends on unsigned wraparound and int truncation

verdicts.claim: The record read in both getById helpers trusts footer offsets: a decreasing pair gives new char[negative], an oversized pair gives an unbounded allocation, and a short read leaves uninitialised bytes that std::string(buffer) scans.
verdicts.evidence: cpp:162-168 and :222-228 (pre-fix): readl = endidx - startidx; new char[readl + 1]; seekg; read; buffer[readl]='\0'; std::string text(buffer). Nothing checked ordering or bounds, or looked at gcount() or the stream state. The offsets come from IndexedMzMLDecoder::stringToStreampos (IndexedMzMLDecoder.cpp:30-66), which accepts any unsigned 64-bit value, so they can be negative as streamoff or lie far past EOF. index_offset_ itself is bounded: parseOffsets returns -1 when indexoffset > file length (IndexedMzMLDecoder.cpp:95-100), so parsing_success_ is false in that case and the helpers throw before reading. There was a second silent defect: a short read sets failbit, and the stream was never cleared, so every later seekg/read on that handler became a no-op returning garbage.
verdicts.change: Added an anonymous-namespace helper readRecord_(stream, filename, start, end, index_offset), used by both helpers. It throws Exception::ParseError (with OPENMS_PRETTY_FUNCTION) unless 0 <= start <= end <= index_offset_. Records always come before <indexList>, and index_offset_ was already checked against the file length, so allocation is capped by the file size with no extra I/O. The helper clears the stream state before seeking, reads into a value-initialised std::string (no new[]/delete[]), shrinks it to gcount(), and clears the state again. A short read is truncated rather than thrown on purpose: on Windows a text-mode ifstream (filestream_ is opened in text mode) turns CRLF into one character and can legitimately hit EOF on the last record. A record that really is incomplete is now rejected by MzMLSpectrumDecoder, which (in this working tree) installs a throwing Xerces error handler. I left out an arbitrary fixed size ceiling because it would reject legitimately large chromatograms and imaging spectra, and the file-size bound already stops unbounded allocation from a small hostile file. I checked the helper's std semantics (fpos/streamoff conversions, seek after a short read, zero-length range) with a standalone clang++ -std=c++20 program using stub exceptions. The OpenMS build was not run.
verdicts.regression_risk: Moderate-low. Files whose index lists a record offset after <indexList>, or in decreasing order, now throw ParseError. Before, they threw std::bad_array_new_length or returned garbage. Valid files read exactly the same bytes. Text containing an embedded NUL is no longer cut at the NUL, but such text is not valid XML either way.

verdicts.claim: ImzMLWriter::store calls startProgress but only calls endProgress on success, so any throw in between leaves ProgressLogger's recursion depth raised.
verdicts.evidence: ImzMLWriter.cpp store(): logger.startProgress(0, work.size() + 2, ...) (now line 1479), then UnableToCreateFile, writer ParseErrors, the fflush ParseError and writeImzMLXml_'s UnableToCreateFile could all throw before the single logger.endProgress() at the end. ProgressLogger.h:105 declares 'static int recursion_depth_', and ProgressLogger.cpp:238/266-268 raise and lower it. The depth is shared across the whole process, so the leak affects every later progress output.
verdicts.change: Wrapped everything after startProgress in try { ... } catch (...) { logger.endProgress(); ...; throw; }, with the normal endProgress() after the try. I chose try/catch over an RAII guard so endProgress() (not noexcept) never runs from a destructor during unwinding. A comment gives the reason. No class test: a failure after startProgress needs a mid-write I/O error (or more than 1e8 array elements), which the class-test framework cannot trigger portably.
verdicts.regression_risk: None on success. On failure, progress output is now closed before the exception propagates.

verdicts.claim: A failed ImzMLWriter::store leaves a truncated .ibd behind with no .imzML.

UniqueFile_ only calls fclose (around line 812), so a partial .ibd survived.

A pre-existing .ibd is never deleted when this call could not even open the path. UniqueFile_'s inner scope has already closed the handle when the catch runs, so the removal also works on Windows. Uses the existing OpenMS::File::remove helper (added #include <OpenMS/SYSTEM/File.h>). Documented in ImzMLFile.h store(), including that an earlier .ibd at the same path is overwritten once writing starts and is not restored. No class test, for the same reason as CPP-133.
verdicts.regression_risk: Only failed stores change: the .ibd this call created is removed instead of left truncated. writeImzMLXml_ throws only before it writes any bytes (the failed ofstream open), so no partial .imzML needs cleaning. Successful stores are unchanged.

verdicts.claim: The two buildImagingGeometry overloads, documented as the same source of truth, disagree on when the pixel size is copied and on which skip reason is checked first.

The index overload requires meta.pixel_size_x > 0 && meta.pixel_size_y > 0 (line 468). verdicts.claim: ImzMLHandler's fill for a spectrum with only one external array never runs: MzMLHandler throws first on the mismatched decoded sizes.

It fills the non-external side from decoded peaks at lines 228-231 (mz_vec[i] = s[i].getMZ()) and 241-244 (int_vec[i] = s[i].getIntensity()). For such a spectrum, the inline array decodes N values and the external <binary/> placeholder decodes 0. MzMLHandler.cpp:410-414 compares these decoded sizes and calls fatalError(LOAD, "The length of m/z and integer values ... differ"), which throws ParseError before consumeSpectrum. OnDiscImzMLExperiment::open would reject such a file at open time instead of at getSpectrum, with the same exception type (ParseError).

verdicts.claim: ImzMLWriter::store skips a mis-sized FloatDataArray under default options but aborts when a PeakFileOptions sort or m/z/intensity filter actually touches the spectrum.
verdicts.evidence: Confirmed. appendAndWriteFloatDataArrays_ skips an array whose fda.size() != spec.size() with a warning ('Per-peak contract'). applyStoreOptions_ runs first and calls spectrum.sortByPosition() in both branches and spectrum.select(kept). MSSpectrum.cpp:444-460 sortByPosition goes through sort() whenever data arrays exist. MSSpectrum.h:365-369 sort() calls checkDataArraySizes_(), and so does MSSpectrum.cpp:66 selectUnchecked (reached from select). checkDataArraySizes_ (MSSpectrum.cpp:20-38) throws Exception::Precondition for any mis-sized float, string or integer array. PeakFileOptions.h:241 defaults sort_spectra_by_mz_ = true, so even default options abort on an unsorted spectrum.
verdicts.change: Added dropMisalignedDataArrays_(MSExperiment&) in ImzMLWriter.cpp. It removes every non-empty float, integer or string data array whose length differs from the peak count, and warns once per array with the same text appendAndWriteFloatDataArrays_ used. applyStoreOptions_ calls it after the spectrum-level filters (MS level, RT, precursor), so only spectra that will be stored are checked, and before any sort or select. A comment explains why. The kernel preconditions are untouched. The check in appendAndWriteFloatDataArrays_ stays as a guard at the write, with its comment updated. Integer and string arrays are included because checkDataArraySizes_ refuses them too and imzML discards them anyway. New test section 'void store skips a misaligned FloatDataArray whatever the PeakFileOptions say': one unsorted 2-peak spectrum with a 1-value array, stored under no-sort, default-sort and m/z-trimming options. Each must store and reload without the array (2, 2 and 1 peaks).
verdicts.regression_risk: Stores that used to abort with Precondition now succeed and skip the array. Stores that already succeeded write the same files with the same FloatDataArray warning text, emitted slightly earlier. A mis-sized integer or string array now gets its own 'Skipping IntegerDataArray/StringDataArray' line and is no longer counted in the aggregate 'dropping N integer/string data array(s)' warning.

verdicts.claim: In the linear x/y/z suffix branch, the loss helper gets the m/z (pos) instead of the charged mass, so charge is divided out twice: (M/z - L)/z instead of (M - L)/z.
verdicts.evidence: The claim held. TheoreticalSpectrumGeneratorXLMS.cpp:305 sets `double pos(mono_weight / static_cast<double>(charge))`, and :311 (before the fix) called `addLinearIonLosses_(..., pos, ...)`. The helper at :567-571 and :586-590 computes `mass_with_loss = mono_weight - loss_H2O_` and then `setMZ(mass_with_loss / charge)`. The header TheoreticalSpectrumGeneratorXLMS.h:185 documents that argument as the 'monoisotopic mass of the current ion'. The prefix branch at :277, and all four cross-link loss calls (:487, :527, :1038, :1081), already pass mono_weight. Worked example from the report (KS, link_pos 0, y1 of S, z=2): the intact peak is at 53.5286; the buggy water-loss peak was at 17.7590; the correct one is at 44.5233.
verdicts.change: Line 312 now passes `mono_weight` instead of `pos` to addLinearIonLosses_ in the suffix branch, matching the prefix branch. I added a one-line comment explaining why (the helper subtracts the loss and divides by charge itself). I did not add a test: TheoreticalSpectrumGeneratorXLMS_test.cpp is not in this group's owned_files. A suggested test is in the notes.
verdicts.regression_risk: Only suffix loss peaks move, and only at charge >= 2 with add_losses=true. The emptiness filter `mass_with_loss > 0.0` now tests M-L instead of M/z-L. Every peak it kept before it still keeps, so the peak count cannot drop. It can only grow at very high charge (y1 of S first at z>=7). In TheoreticalSpectrumGeneratorXLMS_test.cpp the exact-m/z arrays run with add_losses=false. The loss sections (IFSQVGK, link 3, z<=3; expected counts 30 and 48, charge counts 10/10/10) check counts and names only, and every suffix loss there already passed the old filter (x1(K) z=3: M/3=58.37 > 17.03). None of those expectations change. XQuestScores_test, OPXLHelper_test and OPXLSpectrumProcessingAlgorithms_test run with add_losses=false. OpenPepXLAlgorithm (:348, ions:neutral_losses defaults to true; :625/:630 build linear spectra at charge 2) now builds correct charge-2 suffix loss peaks for its scoring after the main score. verdicts.claim: PercolatorInfile::load looks up the merge index for filename "UNKNOWN" with an unchecked .at(), so a PIN without a FileName column throws std::out_of_range.

verdicts.claim: stampPinFeaturesOnHits computes enzN/enzC from PeptideEvidence's raw '['/']' protein-terminus markers, and only converts them to '-' later for the Peptide string.

verdicts.claim: The writer puts multiple proteins in tab-separated trailing fields, but load() rejects any row wider than the header and only splits Proteins on ';'.
verdicts.evidence: src/openms/source/FORMAT/PercolatorInfile.cpp (pre-edit): line 549 stamps Proteins as `ListUtils::concatenate(proteins, "\t")`, and preparePin_ (line 595) joins features with tabs, so a PSM with two proteins gets one more field than the header.
