Percolator_subprocess_parity_test.cpp:397 also notes that Proteins "embeds tabs and inflates the split count". The writer is correct. The reader is the problem: line 239 threw ParseError whenever `row.size() != pin_header.size()`, and line 313 only split row[Proteins] on ';' (Sage's convention, see sage.pin test data). So load() rejected OpenMS's own store() output, and other spec-compliant PINs, as soon as a PSM mapped to more than one protein.
verdicts.change: load() now reads Proteins as a variable-width last column when the header's last column is "Proteins" (flag proteins_trailer). Such rows may be wider than the header. Shorter rows, and wider rows when Proteins is not last, still throw the same ParseError. Accessions are collected from every field from the Proteins column to the end of the row, and each field is still split on ';' so Sage files keep working. On-disk formats are unchanged.
verdicts.regression_risk: sage.pin has 34 fields per row, matching the header, with Proteins last and ';'-joined, so it parses exactly as before and the existing load test expectations (9 pids, 2 filenames, decoy relabel) still hold. One trade-off: if a file has Proteins as its last column and a row has an extra tab somewhere earlier, that row used to be rejected and is now accepted, with the extra field read as an accession. Percolator's own PIN reader has the same ambiguity.

verdicts.claim: SVOutStream's manipulator probe buffer is only cleared after a bare "\n", so after std::ends (or any manipulator that writes something else) no later std::endl is recognised and every following line starts with a separator.

b

verdicts.claim: When loading TrafoXML, a <Param> with an unsupported type attribute only logs a non-fatal error and the parameter is dropped.

verdicts.claim: TransformationModelLinear reads symmetric_regression into symmetric_ but never uses it, so the documented regression of y-x on y+x is never performed.

Actually implementing symmetric regression (u=y+x, v=y-x, fit v=a*u+b, then slope=(1+a)/(1-a), intercept=b/(1-a), throwing UnableToFit when a is 1) should be a separate, deliberate behaviour change with a CHANGELOG entry and new test expectations.

verdicts.claim: DataValue's operator long double/double/float reject only EMPTY_VALUE and handle INT_VALUE. For String and list values they return data_.dou_, which reads an inactive union member (undefined behaviour) when the documented contract says ConversionError.
verdicts.evidence: Confirmed in the pre-edit source. DataValue.cpp:452-492: each floating operator threw only for EMPTY_VALUE (454/468/482), returned the int for INT_VALUE (459/473/487) and otherwise ended in `return data_.dou_;` (463/477/491). The union at DataValue.h:409-417 keeps std::string*/StringList*/IntList*/DoubleList* for STRING_VALUE and the list types; the constructors at DataValue.cpp:118-146 set exactly those pointer members, so reading dou_ reinterprets a heap pointer. DataValue.h:112 and the per-operator @exception lines (then 164/173/182) promise ConversionError for a wrong type. The integer siblings at DataValue.cpp:494-592 already throw when value_type_ != INT_VALUE. The mzML caller is still live: MzMLHandler.cpp:1414-1416 calls `spec_.setRT(spec_.getMetaValue("elution time (seconds)"))`. A userParam of that name is typed by fromXSDString (MzMLHandler.cpp:3436), so it can be a STRING_VALUE. ParamValue.cpp:384-421 has the same pattern, but that is outside this finding and these files.

The message follows the integer siblings. A comment at DataValue.cpp:452-457 says why: the union holds pointers for those types, and strings are not parsed. The existing EMPTY_VALUE branch and its message are unchanged, because DataValue_test.cpp:1003-1016 checks that message by exact string equality (ClassTest.h:950). INT_VALUE and DOUBLE_VALUE behave as before. The header docs for the three operators (DataValue.h:159-187) now say that DOUBLE_VALUE and INT_VALUE are accepted, that a numeric-looking STRING_VALUE is not parsed, and that ConversionError is thrown for String, lists and Empty. I added no class test because DataValue_test.cpp is not in this group's owned_files; the test I propose is in notes.
verdicts.regression_risk: Only String and list values change: they used to give an undefined value (on 64-bit, usually a pointer read as a tiny subnormal number close to 0) and now throw ConversionError. Numeric and Empty conversions are unchanged, including the EMPTY messages that are asserted exactly. TEST_REAL_SIMILAR on a DataValue goes through operator long double (ClassTest.h testRealSimilar takes long double). I checked every test that compares a meta value to 0 that way: SiriusFragmentAnnotation 'decoy' (a bool stored as Int), RTAlignment 'rt_raw', IsobaricChannelExtractor 'precursor_intensity', ConfidenceScoring 'GLM_score'/'local_FDR', MRMFeatureSelector 'peak_apex_int', MRMFeatureFilter QC scores. All are numeric, so none was passing by accident. The imzML pixel-size and max-dim keys are always stored as double (ImzMLFile.cpp:130-142, 524-525). Callers that can now throw where they used to get garbage: (a) the MzMLHandler.cpp:1416 elution-time fallback, if a file has a string userParam 'elution time (seconds)' and no scan start time, so loading fails; (b) DataFilters::metaPasses_ (DataFilters.cpp:462), whose numeric filter excludes only STRING/EMPTY, so a list-valued meta value now throws; (c) ImzMLWriter::store via extractMeta_ (ImzMLWriter.cpp:359-373), which throws before any file is opened (it runs at 1455, before the write plans). None of these paths is exercised by the existing DataFilters, MzMLFile or ImzMLFile tests.

verdicts.claim: A duplicate of CPP-058 at the imzML call site: ImzMLWriter extractMeta_ casts imzml:pixel_size_x/y and max_dim_x/y with static_cast<double>. For a String meta value this reads the union's pointer bits, so the file gets a nonsense pixel size and IMS:1000044/45 extent instead of a ConversionError.

verdicts.claim: Short design rows are read out of range: the one-table width check runs after the cells are read, the two-table sample section has no width check, and both SampleSection::getFactorValue overloads index the row unchecked.

Before the change, ExperimentalDesignFile.cpp:232-234 read cells[...Label], [...Fraction] and [...Fraction_Group] with operator[], and :247 read [...Sample]. The only check, parseErrorIf_(n_col != cells.size()), came afterwards at :248. With header 'Fraction_Group\tFraction\tSpectra_Filepath\tLabel\tSample' and row '1\t1\ta.mzML', Label index 3 is past the end of the 3-cell row. In the two-table SAMPLE_CONTENT branch (:421-430), n_col was set at :418 but never compared. The branch read cells[sample_columnname_to_columnindex_["Sample"]] and pushed the row, short or not, into sample_content_. In ExperimentalDesign.cpp:982-984 and :1005-1007, both overloads bounds-check the row with content_.at() and then read sample_row[col_index] unchecked. That is the exception the same functions already throw for an unknown sample or factor, and it follows the branch's existing switch from bare std::out_of_range to OpenMS exceptions (see getSampleName). Each site has a short comment saying why. I added no test because this group owns no test file; suggested tests are in notes.

The one-table parser accepts the same rows, because raw width equal to header width is the same condition the old post-append check tested. New behaviour: (1) a two-table sample row whose width differs from its header is now a ParseError at load instead of being stored. This includes rows that lost a trailing empty cell to line trimming, which used to fail only if that factor was ever read. verdicts.change: ExperimentalDesignFile.cpp: the one-table parser now rejects label/fraction/fraction_group < 0 with parseErrorIf_ right after they are read (:243-245), before the 'Label > 1' check and before assignment. verdicts.claim: A reused MzMLValidator keeps referenceableParamGroup terms (and binary-array state) from earlier documents, so a later document's dangling group reference can satisfy mapping rules.
verdicts.evidence: MzMLValidator.h:66-74 declares param_groups_, current_id_, binary_data_array_ and binary_data_type_ as members. MzMLValidator.cpp fills param_groups_[current_id_] (old line 83) and reads param_groups_[ref] (old line 50). Nothing ever cleared them. The inherited SemanticValidator::validate (SemanticValidator.cpp:142-171) resets errors_, warnings_, open_tags_ and fulfilled_ (the last two are the validators group's working-tree change at 155-160), but it cannot see the derived members. XMLHandler::reset() (XMLHandler.h:78) is non-virtual and empty, so no per-parse hook exists that a derived class could override. The claim holds. It is reachable only through direct reuse of the public class: MzMLFile::isSemanticallyValid (MzMLFile.cpp:113-124) builds a fresh validator on every call, and MzMLHandler/MSDataWritingConsumer use the validator only for locateTerm during writing.
verdicts.change: In MzMLValidator::onStartElement (MzMLValidator.cpp:41-52) I added an else branch. When open_tags_ is empty, the element is the document element of a new file, and the branch clears param_groups_, current_id_, binary_data_array_ and binary_data_type_ there. A comment explains that groups belong to the document that defines them. This is the only reset point available without editing the header, which I do not own. It is exact: open_tags_ is pushed on every start and popped on every end (SemanticValidator.cpp:177/289), so it is empty only before the root opens. Well-formed XML has no elements after the root closes. It also holds after an aborted parse, because validate() now clears open_tags_ first. Repeated definitions and forward references within one document behave as before. No test was added because I own no class test file (see notes).
verdicts.regression_risk: Only code that validates several files with one MzMLValidator and relied on groups carrying over between files is affected; nothing in the tree does that. Single-document validation is unchanged. The failed-parse case depends on the validators group's open_tags_.clear() in SemanticValidator::validate staying in. Without it, a parse aborted mid-document leaves open_tags_ non-empty and the reset would not fire. The validator is unreliable in that state anyway (CPP-040).

verdicts.claim: MzMLFile::isValid chooses between the plain and indexed mzML schema by looking for '<indexedmzML' in the first four trimmed lines, so a legal prolog pushes the root past line four and the wrong schema is used.
verdicts.evidence: MzMLFile.cpp:62-64 (before the change): TextFile file(filename, true, 4); s = concatenate(file); indexed = hasSubstring(s, "<indexedmzML"). TextFile::load (TextFile.cpp:54-75) stops after first_n buffered lines, and skip_empty_lines/comment_symbol are left at their defaults, so blank and comment lines count toward the four. Three comment lines after the XML declaration therefore select mzML_1_10.xsd, which does not declare indexedmzML. The same predicate has two more failures. A comment containing '<indexedmzML' ahead of an mzML root selects the indexed schema. A file written on one line is loaded whole into memory. TextFile itself matches its documentation (TextFile.h:49-51), so the defect is in the caller.
verdicts.change: In MzMLFile.cpp I replaced the line sniffing. A file-local RootElementHandler_ (a subclass of Internal::XMLHandler) records the qname of the first start element and throws XMLHandler::EndParsingSoftly, the same early-stop idiom MzMLHandler and FeatureXMLHandler use. isValid runs it through the existing XMLFile::parse_, which handles the prolog, comments, PIs, BOM/encodings and compressed input, and stops at the root start tag. A namespace prefix is stripped, because parse_ runs without namespace processing. The indexed schema is chosen iff the local name is 'indexedmzML'. An Exception::ParseError, meaning the file is not well-formed before its root, is caught, and the plain schema is used so that XMLValidator reports the actual error as before. FileNotFound still propagates, matching the documented contract. I removed the now-unused TextFile.h include. The comment says why lines are no longer inspected. TextFile.h/.cpp are unchanged. No test was added because I own no class test file (see notes).
verdicts.regression_risk: Schema choice is unchanged for any file whose root name was in the first four lines, which covers the existing MzMLFile_test isValid cases (stored plain/indexed files and MzMLFile_4_indexed.mzML). For a file that is malformed before its root, isValid still returns false, but XMLHandler::fatalError now also writes one OPENMS_LOG_FATAL_ERROR line. For an existing but unreadable file, fatalError's FileHandler::getTypeByContent uses TextFile and throws FileNotReadable, as the old code did. XMLValidator still reads raw bytes, so compressed mzML still fails validation, as before.

verdicts.claim: The KEY_ID_IDX/FKNID identity constraints in mzML_idx_1_10.xsd select nothing (they look for an indexedmzML below the indexedmzML they are declared on) and the keyref reads @id instead of @idRef, so dangling index offsets pass schema validation.
verdicts.evidence: share/OpenMS/SCHEMAS/mzML_idx_1_10.xsd:1192-1199 declares both constraints on the indexedmzML element (1166). The key selector is './/dx:indexedmzML/dx:mzML/dx:run/dx:spectrumList/dx:spectrum | .//dx:indexedmzML/dx:mzML/dx:run/dx:chromatogramList/dx:chromatogram'. The keyref selector is './/dx:indexedmzML/dx:indexList/dx:index/dx:offset' with field '@id', but OffsetType (1147-1155) has only the attribute 'idRef'. Compare the mzML element's own keys at 889-906, which use root-relative './dx:run/...'. I checked this in the scratchpad with xmllint. MzMLFile_4_indexed.mzML with idRef="index=19" changed to "does_not_exist" validates against the shipped schema. Against a copy with the corrected selectors and field it fails with 'No match found for key-sequence [does_not_exist] of keyref FKNID'. The claim holds.
verdicts.change: No edit. The hard constraints forbid editing anything under share/OpenMS/, even though the file appears in this group's owned_files. The exact edit is recorded in needs_shared_file. Impact on reference data, measured with xmllint on all 22 files containing '<indexedmzML' under src/tests/class_tests/openms/data: none changes pass/fail status. 14 validate before and after, and 8 fail before and after. Two of the already-failing files gain extra duplicate-key messages: Deisotoper_output2.mzML (a duplicate spectrum id, which already violates KEY_SPECTRUM_ID) and OpenPepXL_input.mzML (a duplicate 'TIC' chromatogram, which already violates KEY_CHROMATOGRAM_ID). No reference document is invalidated.
verdicts.regression_risk: If applied, XSD 1.0 selectors cannot filter on index/@name, so the key has to be one union over spectra and chromatograms. It would then also reject a document in which a spectrum and a chromatogram share an id, which mzML itself allows (the ids are keyed separately at 889-906); none of the 22 in-tree indexed files has such an overlap. Offsets and the file checksum still need separate integrity checks. The schema appears to be a vendored copy of the PSI indexed-mzML schema, so the upstream copy likely carries the same defect.

verdicts.claim: MzIdentMLHandler::writePeptideHit writes a C-terminal modification at location=N (the last residue) instead of the mzIdentML C-terminus location N+1.
verdicts.evidence: Before the fix, MzIdentMLHandler.cpp:1366 wrote `location="" + toStr(hit.getSequence().size())`. The XL-MS writer had the same bug at :1761 (`peptide_sequence.size()`), and the beta-peptide C_TERM cross-link at :1939 wrote `size() + 2`. The claim holds. Four things show N+1 is the C-terminus: (1) the only loader in use (MzIdentMLFile.cpp:38, MzIdentMLDOMHandler) reads `index == aas.size() + 1` as C-terminal (MzIdentMLDOMHandler.cpp:2651, 2748, 2813, 2903) and `index-1 == size` as a C_TERM cross-link (:1904, :1934). (2) The DOM writer uses size()+1 (:3024). (3) The header documents 'peptide_length + 1 = C-terminus' (MzIdentMLDOMHandler.h:131). (4) The Mascot 1.3 reference file MzIdentML_v1.3_xlink_edc.mzid:441/454 writes location="8" for the C-terminus of the 7-residue QLVQDEA. So on reload, an old-writer location=N went to `aas.setModification(N-1, name)` (:2913). For a C-term-only mod such as Amidated, ResidueDB::getModifiedResidue's ANYWHERE lookup fails, the exception is caught and only a warning is logged (:2917), so the mod is lost. Mods that also have a residue variant ended up on the last residue. For the beta cross-link, location=N+2 fails the range check (:2546). inferModificationLocation_ then returns -1 because residues="K", the acceptor is skipped, and `xl_id_acceptor_map_.at()` (:1918) throws std::out_of_range out of load().
verdicts.change: MzIdentMLHandler.cpp: now writes `size() + 1` in writePeptideHit (:1368) and writeXLMSPeptideHit (:1764). The beta C_TERM cross-link location changed from `size() + 2` to `size() + 1` (:1944), matching the alpha branch's `i + 2` with i = last residue index. The unused SAX reader check in handleCVParam_ (:486) now also treats size()+1 as C-terminal, so the file agrees with itself. Each site has a short comment explaining why. I could not add a class test because I own no test file.
verdicts.regression_risk: Changes written mzIdentML only for peptides with C-terminal modifications or C-terminal beta cross-links. It invalidates 0 reference files. Of the 11 .mzid files under src/tests/class_tests/openms/data/, the two written by OpenMS (MzIdentML_XLMS_labelled/unlabelled) carry only internal modifications. The location==length entries in MzIdentML_v1.3_multi_spectra/xlink_edc are genuine last-residue mods from other producers, and the SAX writer does not touch them. MzIdentMLFile_test store sections are store/load round trips, and none of their inputs has a C-terminal mod, so their results do not change. The handleCVParam_ change has no runtime effect: MzIdentMLFile::load uses the DOM handler, and that function looks for 'location' on the cvParam, which mzIdentML never puts there. Files written earlier by OpenMS keep location=N and still load as before (the mod is lost or put on the last residue, with a warning).

verdicts.claim: MzIdentMLDOMHandler::parsePeptideSiblings_ dereferences getFirstChild() of an empty PeptideSequence element (null).
verdicts.evidence: Before the fix, MzIdentMLDOMHandler.cpp:2469-2470 did `DOMNode* tn = element_sib->getFirstChild(); if (tn->getNodeType() == DOMNode::TEXT_NODE)` with no null check. Xerces creates no text node for `<PeptideSequence/>` or `<PeptideSequence></PeptideSequence>`, so tn is nullptr and the process crashes. The caller's catch(...) at :776 cannot catch a null dereference. A comment as the first child also threw 'Non Text Node' and lost a valid sequence. The same file already reads <Seq> text with `child->getTextContent()` (:727). The only caller, parsePeptideElements_ (:762-779), already handles unreadable Peptides: it logs 'No amino acid sequence readable from Peptide' and stores an empty AASequence.
verdicts.change: The sequence is now read with `StringManager::convert(element_sib->getTextContent())` (:2471). That returns "" for an empty element and ignores comments. The trim moved from before step 3 to right after reading (:2476), so substitution locations count residues rather than pretty-printing whitespace. An empty or missing sequence now throws Exception::ParseError(..., OPENMS_PRETTY_FUNCTION, ...) (:2479-2482). That goes through the existing catch(...) path (logged error, empty AASequence) instead of applying substitutions and modifications to an empty string.
verdicts.regression_risk: Valid files behave the same. I checked all 10 loadable reference .mzid files: every Peptide has a non-empty, unpadded PeptideSequence. The only file without one is Mascot_MSMS_example.mzid, which is mzIdentML 1.0 with a lowercase <peptideSequence>. Its load is commented out (MzIdentMLFile_test.cpp:369-370) and nothing else loads it. Peptides without a sequence now log one error each and get an empty sequence with no modifications. Before, they also got an empty sequence but modifications were half-applied to it (and CPP-169's out-of-bounds write could run). A PeptideSequence containing a comment now parses instead of coming back empty.

verdicts.claim: The SubstitutionModification 'location' is used unchecked as a string index (location 0 or > length writes out of bounds), and the residue attributes are not checked for being empty.
verdicts.evidence: Before the fix, MzIdentMLDOMHandler.cpp:2500 did `as[StringUtils::toInt32(location) - 1] = replacementResidue;` with no range check. For location="0" the int -1 becomes size_type SIZE_MAX, and location > as.size() also writes past the end. Both are undefined behaviour in std::string::operator[]. It was reachable even with an empty `as`: the 1.0 Mascot reference file has `<SubstitutionModification location="7" .../>` on a Peptide whose sequence the DOM reader cannot find. `StringManager::convert(...)[0]` on an empty replacementResidue returns '\0' (defined behaviour for reading), but that NUL was then written into the sequence. A non-numeric location already throws ConversionError from StringUtilsHelper::toInt32, which is caught at :776.
verdicts.change: The 1-based position is now checked as `1 <= pos <= as.size()` before indexing, and a violation throws Exception::ParseError with OPENMS_PRETTY_FUNCTION (:2508-2514). An empty replacementResidue is rejected the same way before either branch uses it (:2496-2502). originalResidue is only used in the no-location branch, which already rejects a missing match, so I did not make it required: files that omit it but give a location still load. Because the sequence is now trimmed before substitutions (see CPP-168), the bound applies to the real residue count. Each check has a WHY comment.
verdicts.regression_risk: None for well-formed input. No loadable reference .mzid contains a SubstitutionModification; the only one is in the unloaded 1.0 Mascot example. A malformed substitution now makes that Peptide unreadable (logged error, empty sequence) through the existing catch(...) path, the same as the existing no-location, no-match case. Before, it was undefined behaviour.

verdicts.claim: MascotXMLHandler accepts a peptide query number one past <NumQueries> (guard uses > on a 0-based index) and subtracts before validating.
verdicts.evidence: Before the fix, MascotXMLHandler.cpp:56-62 did `peptide_identification_index_ = attribute_value - 1; if (peptide_identification_index_ > id_data_.size()) fatalError(...)`. id_data_ is sized by <NumQueries> (line 80). With NumQueries=1 and <peptide query="2"> the index is 1, `1 > 1` is false, and the next pep_exp_mz / pep_scan_title / pep_homol / pep_ident / </peptide> does id_data_[1] out of bounds (old lines 88, 97, 148, 157, 541). The subtraction `attribute_value - 1` also ran before any check, so INT_MIN overflowed a signed int. The same class of defect exists for <query number>: id_data_[actual_query_ - 1] was used in <StringTitle> (old 342/363/365/370) and <RTINSECONDS> (old 376) with no range check at all, and the constructor (old 17-21) never initialised actual_query_. fatalError throws Exception::ParseError (XMLHandler.cpp:41-69).
verdicts.change: MascotXMLHandler.cpp:57-64 now checks the 1-based value before subtracting: `if (attribute_value <= 0 || static_cast<Size>(attribute_value) > id_data_.size()) fatalError(...)`, then assigns the index. The existing message is kept. Added the same range check (`actual_query_ == 0 || actual_query_ > id_data_.size()`) at the two places where <query number> is first used as an index, <StringTitle> (line 343) and <RTINSECONDS> (line 387), and initialised actual_query_(0) in the constructor (line 19, declaration order kept). The checks sit where the index is used, not on the <query> start tag, so a <query> that has neither child still loads as before. Comments explain the 1-based / one-past-end reasoning.
verdicts.regression_risk: Only inputs that used to index outside id_data_ (undefined behaviour) now throw ParseError. None of the reference inputs trip the new checks. MascotXMLFile_test_1: NumQueries 3, query and number values 1..3. test_2: NumQueries 1120, queries 1..1120, including 1082 u_/q_peptide elements. test_3: NumQueries 17169, highest query 17154; its only zero attribute is <warning number="0">, which is not checked. None of the three contains RTINSECONDS, and StringTitle appears only inside <query>. No reference file changes.

verdicts.claim: The pep_scan_title RT check uses !getRT(), which flags a valid RT of 0 and lets a missing (NaN) RT through.
verdicts.evidence: MascotXMLHandler.cpp old line 117: `if (!id_data_[peptide_identification_index_].getRT())`. PeptideIdentification's rt_ starts as quiet_NaN (PeptideIdentification.cpp:28), and hasRT() is `!std::isnan(rt_)` (lines 64-66). SpectrumMetaData::rt also starts as NaN (SpectrumMetaDataLookup.h:148), and getSpectrumMetaData(const std::string&, ...) returns without touching meta when no reference format matches (SpectrumMetaDataLookup.cpp:73-154). So setRT(meta.rt) stores NaN. `!NaN` is false, so the missing-RT message was never logged. `!0.0` is true, so a real RT of 0 (e.g. title "500.1_0" with the default `^(?<MZ>..)_(?<RT>..)` format) was wrongly reported. The <StringTitle> branch next to it already uses hasRT() (old line 365).
verdicts.change: Line 120 now reads `if (!id_data_[peptide_identification_index_].hasRT())`, with a comment that a failed look-up leaves NaN and 0 is a valid RT.
verdicts.regression_risk: Only log output changes. XMLHandler::error() just writes OPENMS_LOG_ERROR and does not throw (XMLHandler.cpp:71-86), and the message is still printed at most once per file (no_rt_error_). Files whose titles don't give an RT now get that one message. Files with RT 0 no longer do. Loaded data and the MissingInformation throw in MascotXMLFile::load, which already counts with hasRT(), are unchanged. MascotXMLFile_test.cpp does not check log output.

verdicts.claim: The MGF loader reuses one spectrum object and clears only some fields, so RT, precursor and other metadata carry over into later BEGIN IONS blocks that omit them.
verdicts.evidence: Before the fix, MascotGenericFile.h:92-101 built one `spectrum` and set MS level, precursor and type once. getNextSpectrum_ (old 143-154) only did resize(0), setNativeID, and removed TITLE and SEQ. Everything else a block sets stayed on the object and leaked into later blocks that omit it. That covers RTINSECONDS (242-246), PEPMASS m/z and intensity (216-235), CHARGE (236-241), MSLEVEL and its "MSLEVEL" fallback meta value (325-343), and NAME, COMPOUND_NAME, INCHI, SMILES, IONMODE, SOURCE_INSTRUMENT, ORGANISM, PI, DATACOLLECTOR, LIBRARYQUALITY, SPECTRUMID and SCANS (300-378). This is not a header-defaults feature: the outer loop (159-166) skips every line outside BEGIN IONS, so values can only leak from the previous block, which the MGF spec does not allow. Per-query intent is already stated for SEQ ("do not let it bleed across spectra") and tested (MascotGenericFile_test.cpp, "SEQ must not bleed across spectra").
verdicts.change: getNextSpectrum_ (MascotGenericFile.h:145-153) now starts each block with `spectrum.clear(true)`, the MSSpectrum API already used this way in BrukerTimsFile.cpp. It resets peaks, data arrays, SpectrumSettings including all meta values and precursors, RT, drift time and MS level. It then re-applies the MGF defaults (MS level 2, one precursor, CENTROID, native ID). That replaces the TITLE/SEQ removals and the one-off setup in load() (line 97 now just declares the object). A comment explains why the reset has to be complete. The class docs (lines 39-42) now say each block is independent and header parameters outside blocks are not applied. The MGF writer is untouched, so the on-disk format does not change.
verdicts.regression_risk: The first block loads exactly as before: clear(true) restores the default-constructor values (retention_time_ -1, drift_time_ -1 == IMTypes::DRIFTTIME_NOT_SET, ms_level 1, then set to 2). Only the second and later blocks change, and only for fields they omit. Every MGF input in the test data has one BEGIN IONS block (FileHandler_MGFbyContent1/2.mgf, MascotGenericFile_GNPS.mgf, MascotInfile_test.mascot_in), and the multi-block SEQ bleed test expects exactly this reset, so no expected value moves. This reduced Core SDK has no TOPP or pyOpenMS MGF consumers. Users who relied on the leak (later blocks inheriting RT or charge) now get defaults, which is the fix. Cost: shrink_to_fit inside clear(true) adds a few small reallocations per block, negligible next to text parsing, and addSpectrum copies the spectrum anyway.

verdicts.claim: ClassTest::isRealSimilar treats any two infinities as similar, so TEST_REAL_SIMILAR(inf, -inf) passes.
verdicts.evidence: Before the fix, src/testframework/source/CONCEPT/ClassTest.cpp:374-383 rejected only NaN. For (inf, -inf), absdiff = inf - (-inf) is +inf, not NaN as the log says, but ratio = inf / -inf is NaN (old :440). So 'ratio < 0.' (:441), 'ratio < 1.' (:458) and 'ratio > ratio_max_allowed' (:467) were all false, and control reached the final else at :483, which returns true with 'ratio of numbers is small'. (inf, inf) took the same path. The finite-against-infinite case (1.0, -inf) also passed, through the -0.0 path described in CPP-139. I confirmed this with a transcription of the old control flow (old=1 for inf,-inf / -inf,inf / 1,-inf), then by linking a driver against the edited ClassTest.cpp. The log's proposed fix (reject every non-finite argument) would break 12 existing assertions that compare a result with the same infinity and currently pass: AbsoluteQuantitation_test.cpp:193,212; MRMFeatureFilter_test.cpp:119,139; FeatureDistance_test.cpp:115,150; TransformationModel_test.cpp:123,126,129,132,135,138. FuzzyStringComparator.cpp:588-599 already sets the precedent that equal infinities are accepted and every other infinite pair is rejected.
verdicts.change: Added an infinity branch right after the NaN guards (ClassTest.cpp:387-412). Two equal infinities return true ('both numbers are the same infinity'). Any other pair with an infinite operand returns false: 'infinities have different signs' or 'one number is infinite and the other is not'. In that case absdiff and absdiff_max are set to +inf so the failure line shows a meaningful absolute difference. A comment explains why the decision has to come before the arithmetic. Added explicit #include <cmath> and <limits> (they were only reachable through ClassTestUtils.h). A -std=c++20 -Wall -Wextra -fsyntax-only check of the file is clean. A scratch driver linked against the edited file gives: (inf,-inf)=0, (inf,inf)=1, (-inf,-inf)=1, (1,-inf)=0, (-inf,1)=0. No class test added, because ClassTest_test.cpp is not in this group's owned files (see notes).
verdicts.regression_risk: A TEST_REAL_SIMILAR or TEST::isRealSimilar call comparing opposite infinities, or an infinity against a finite value, used to pass whenever it hit the NaN or -0.0 fall-through and will now fail. All 12 call sites that visibly use infinity compare equal infinities and keep passing, and MathFunctions_test.cpp:55-56 compares finite results. A runtime-produced infinity in a data-array comparison (MzMLSqliteHandler_test.cpp and SqMassFile_test.cpp call isRealSimilar directly) could now fail, but that would expose a real mismatch the old code hid. No reference files are involved: failure messages go to stdout, or to a tmp file in ClassTest_test.

verdicts.claim: isRealSimilar reads the opposite-sign case off the quotient. That quotient can underflow to -0.0, so (1e-300, -1e300) and (1.0, -inf) are accepted while the swapped pairs are rejected.
verdicts.evidence: Old ClassTest.cpp:440-441 was 'ratio = number_1 / number_2; if (ratio < 0.)', with ratio a double global (ClassTest.cpp:36). 1e-300 / -1e300 = -1e-600 becomes -0.0 in double. On x86-64 the long double quotient is representable but is truncated to -0.0 when assigned to the double. '-0.0 < 0.' is false, so the else branch runs. 'ratio < 1.' (:458) is true, so ratio = 1. / -0.0 = -inf, and '-inf > ratio_max_allowed' (:467) is false, so the function returns true at :483. The transcribed old flow gives (1e-300,-1e300)=1 but (-1e300,1e-300)=0, and (1e-300,1e300)=0, exactly as the log describes. The comment at old :462 ('by now, we are sure that ratio >= 1') was false on this path. Where the sign test runs, both operands are known to be non-zero: '!number_1' at :431 and '!number_2' at :454 treat -0.0 as zero. After the CPP-138 branch they are also finite, so std::signbit is unambiguous.
verdicts.change: Replaced 'if (ratio < 0.)' with 'if (std::signbit(number_1) != std::signbit(number_2))' (ClassTest.cpp:477), with a comment explaining why the operands are tested rather than the quotient. The quotient is still computed just before the test (:469), so the failure line keeps reporting the relative value as before. With same-sign operands the quotient is now always positive (or +0.0 or +inf), so the 'ratio >= 1' comment at :498 holds again. Verified with a transcription and a driver linked against the edited file: (1e-300,-1e300) now returns false ('numbers have different signs and difference is not small'), matching the swapped pair; (1e-6,-1e-6) still returns true through the small-absdiff path. All 324 combinations of the ClassTest_test.cpp:148+ sign matrix (bases 0/-5/+5, eps 0/-0.1/+0.1, both tolerance settings) give the same result as before.
verdicts.regression_risk: Results change only for opposite-sign, non-zero, finite pairs whose double quotient underflows to -0.0 (magnitude ratio around 1e308 or more). Such pairs used to pass wrongly and now fail. No existing assertion in the tree compares values that far apart; the ClassTest_test sign matrix is unchanged. There is no output-format or reference-data impact.

verdicts.claim: MSstatsFile::storeLFQ uses operator[] on the design's (file, label) maps. A pair the design does not have silently becomes sample row 0, fraction 0 and run 0.
verdicts.evidence: Before the fix, storeLFQ read path_label_to_sample[tpl1], path_label_to_fraction[tpl1], run_map[tpl2] and path_label_to_fractiongroup[tpl1] on non-const maps. operator[] inserts 0 for a missing key. SampleSection::getFactorValue(unsigned) does content_.at(sample_idx) (ExperimentalDesign.cpp:982), so row 0 is read without any error. The earlier guards do not catch this. getNumberOfLabels()!=1 (MSstatsFile.cpp:223) only checks the highest label (ExperimentalDesign.cpp:652-660). isSubsetOf_ (MSstatsFile.cpp:317) compares basenames and ignores the label. A reachable case exists: aggregateInfo_ pushes the raw 0-based channel_id as the LFQ label (MSstatsFile.cpp:109), while every other consumer adds 1 (ConsensusMap.cpp:860-864, storeISO MSstatsFile.cpp:724). So an LFQ consensusXML whose headers carry channel_id=0 looks up (file,0), which no label-1 design has. This path is also queue item FORMAT-OBS-115. storeISO had the same operator[] pattern. A design missing one of the consensusXML's channels gave that channel's intensities the condition, bioreplicate and mixture of row 0, with run "<mix>_0_0".
verdicts.change: In storeLFQ (MSstatsFile.cpp:455-473) and storeISO (726-740), the (file, label) pair is now looked up with find() in path_label_to_sample. If it is missing, the code throws Exception::MissingInformation naming the file and label. The other lookups now use .at(). They cannot miss once the sample lookup succeeds, because all three maps come from pathLabelMapper_ over the same MS-file rows (ExperimentalDesign.cpp:341-361, 556-575) and run_map is built from those rows too (assembleRunMap_). The comment explains why operator[] was wrong. The 0-based channel_id label mapping itself (FORMAT-OBS-115) is not changed. It now fails with an explicit error, which matches the Rust port.
verdicts.regression_risk: Inputs that used to produce mis-attributed rows without warning now throw. Examples: an LFQ consensusXML whose headers carry channel_id, or an ISO design missing a channel. I checked all 14 MSstats reference outputs in packages/test-data/topp (MSstatsConverter_1/2/3/subset_out.csv and ProteomicsLFQ_*_out.csv). None has a Run of "0" (LFQ) or a "_0_0" run (ISO). The LFQ test inputs have no channel_id, and the TMT inputs carry channel_id 0..9 against design labels 1..10, so every lookup resolves. No MSstats reference file exists under core src/tests/class_tests/openms/data.

verdicts.claim: An unknown retention_time_summarization_method in storeLFQ matches no branch, so every aggregated intensity is written as 0 and the CSV is still produced.
verdicts.evidence: constructFile_ sets intensity(0) (MSstatsFile.cpp:182), assigns it only for "max", "min", "mean" and "sum" (184-199), and always writes the line (202-204). storeLFQ only compared the string with "manual" and never checked it otherwise. storeISO is not affected: it forces rt_summarization_manual=true for any value, with a warning, so the aggregating branch is never reached. MSstatsConverter restricts the value with setValidStrings_ (topp/src/MSstatsConverter.cpp:115), and ProteomicsLFQ passes "max" (proteomics-lfq/src/ProteomicsLFQ.cpp:2802). The pyOpenMS binding, however, accepts any string for storeLFQ (pyopenms/bindings/bind_format.cpp:1179), so a bogus name reaches this code.
verdicts.change: storeLFQ now checks the method against manual,max,min,mean,sum with ListUtils::create/ListUtils::contains. For any other value it throws Exception::IllegalArgument, listing the valid values via ListUtils::concatenate. The check runs before any consensus processing (MSstatsFile.cpp:242-250), and a comment says why.
verdicts.regression_risk: Only calls with a name outside the five valid values change: they now throw instead of writing a file of zeros. The match is case-sensitive, and the valid set is the same as MSstatsConverter's. No test or in-tree caller uses another value. storeISO behaviour is unchanged.

verdicts.claim: For "sum" and "mean", constructFile_ collects intensities in a std::set. Equal intensities at different retention times collapse into one value, so 10,10,20 gives sum 30 and mean 15 instead of 40 and 13.33.
verdicts.evidence: constructFile_ drops repeats by retention time on purpose: it keeps a retention_times set and warns on a repeated RT (MSstatsFile.cpp:146-166). It also stored intensities in set<MSstatsFile::Intensity>, which additionally merged different features with the same intensity value. sumIntensity_ and meanIntensity_ (MSstatsFile.h:137-150) then summed and divided over the reduced set. A small copy of the loop run in the scratchpad confirmed this: entries 5@300, 10@100, 10@200 and 20@300 gave sum 15 and mean 7.5 with the set, and 25 and 8.33 with one entry per distinct RT. max and min are not affected. The TOPP help text describes the option as combining peptide ions found at different retention times, so dropping an equal-valued measurement is wrong.
verdicts.change: intensities is now a vector<MSstatsFile::Intensity>, filled once per distinct retention time (MSstatsFile.cpp:148-165). sum and mean use std::accumulate (added #include <numeric>). mean divides by static_cast<Intensity>(size()), the same float division the header helper did. verdicts.claim: TIC/RIC slump percentage is computed as (100 / exp.size()) * count in integer arithmetic, truncating to 0 for runs with more than 100 spectra

verdicts.claim: MzDataHandler::fillData_ reads precisions_[0]/[1] before checking that both arrays exist, and a length mismatch is only logged before the peak loop reads past the shorter arrays.
verdicts.evidence: Checked against the pre-edit source, which matches the report's revision. MzDataHandler.cpp:522 and :527 read precisions_[0] and precisions_[1]. The `data_to_decode_.size() < 2` guard only came at :533, so a spectrum with one binary array read precisions_[1] out of bounds. At :537-541 an m/z vs intensity length mismatch goes to error(LOAD,...), and XMLHandler::error (XMLHandler.cpp:71-87) only writes a log line. :545 then sets peak_count_ to the m/z length, and the loop at :558-561 reads decoded_list_[1][n] past the end of a shorter intensity array. The supplemental-array read at :572 (precisions_[2+i], decoded_*_list_[2+i][n]) had no check on array count or length. This is reachable from OpenMS's own output: writeTo at :1035-1046 logs an error for a FloatDataArray whose length differs from the spectrum and still writes its mda.size() values. The decode loop at :482 reads precisions_[i] for every data_to_decode_ entry, but the two vectors grow on different tags (a <data> start at :409-410; mzArrayBinary, intenArrayBinary and arrayName at :420/:424/:429). A missing or stray <data> therefore reads past precisions_, and onCharacters :142 calls data_to_decode_.back() on an empty vector when a <data> appears before any array. The precision defaults also disagreed: decoding treats anything but "64" as 32-bit (:482), but reading treated anything but "32" as 64-bit (:522/:527), so it could read from the empty list.
verdicts.change: MzDataHandler.cpp, all in the one owned file. (1) :477 fillData_ now first checks that precisions_.size() equals data_to_decode_.size(). If not, it logs error(LOAD) and keeps the spectrum without peaks, because the pairing between arrays and encodings cannot be recovered. (2) :533 the <2-arrays guard now runs before precisions_[0]/[1] are read, with a warning when exactly one array is present (same idea as MzMLHandler:387-395). (3) :545/:550 the primary-array precision test is now `!= "64"`, matching the decode branch. (4) :569 the peak count is also capped at the intensity length. The existing non-fatal error() is kept, so loading stays tolerant but never reads past the end. (5) :598-610 each supplemental array is read only while n is inside its decoded length and the array exists; a short or missing array ends early, as in MzMLHandler:604/:770. (6) :139 onCharacters appends <data> text only when an array slot exists; otherwise the text goes to the existing 'Unhandled character content' warning and check (1) reports the unpaired precision. Each change has a short comment saying why. No test added: MzDataFile_test.cpp is not in this group's owned files (see notes).
verdicts.regression_risk: No change for valid files. A python check of all 10 .mzData files under src/tests/class_tests/openms/data showed the same in every spectrum: m/z array then intensity array, one <data> per array, only 32/64 precision, and equal decoded lengths across all arrays that also match the 'length' attribute. None of the new branches fire for this reference data, and the MzDataFile_test expectations are unaffected. Behaviour changes only for malformed input, all cases that were undefined behaviour before: broken array/<data> pairing now loads the spectrum without peaks and logs an error; a spectrum with one array now has no peaks and a debug warning; a shorter intensity array now truncates the spectrum to that length; a short or missing supplemental array now gives a shorter FloatDataArray; a precision attribute other than 32/64 is now read from the 32-bit decode. The writer and the on-disk format are unchanged.

verdicts.claim: The mzData writer emits ScanMode spellings for ABSORPTION/EMC/TDF that the reader does not recognise, and the reader's fallback changes the previous spectrum (not the current one) for MSn.
verdicts.evidence: Checked against the pre-edit source. writeTo emits value="PhotodiodeArrayDetector" (:919-921), "EnhancedMultiplyChargedScan" (:923-925) and "TimeDelayedFragmentationScan" (:927-929). cvParam_ at :1089-1131 only recognises Zoom, MassScan, SelectedIonDetection, SelectedReactionMonitoring, ConsecutiveReactionMonitoring, ConstantNeutralGainScan, ConstantNeutralLossScan, ProductIonScan, PrecursorIonScan and EnhancedResolutionScan. The fallback at :1134-1136 calls `exp_->getSpectra().back().getInstrumentSettings().setScanMode(MSNSPECTRUM)`. That changes the previous, already-stored spectrum while spec_ keeps UNKNOWN. It is also undefined behaviour when exp_ is still empty: when the first spectrum is MSn, or when earlier spectra were skipped. Skipped spectra are never added (:446-450), and skipping is set by the MS-level filter at :397-400 or the RT filter at :1148-1150. Example: an OpenMS-written file with TDF or EMC MS2 spectra, loaded with setMSLevels({2}), hits back() on an empty vector at the first MS2 spectrum. share/OpenMS/CV/psi-mzdata.obo:223-226 defines PSI:1000036 'Scan Mode' with no fixed value list, so the writer's spellings are legitimate free values. A grep of src/tests and share finds no file using these three spellings; only MassScan (x3) and SelectedIonDetection (x1) occur.
verdicts.change: MzDataHandler.cpp, reader side only. (1) :1170-1183 added three branches that map the writer's spellings back: PhotodiodeArrayDetector to ABSORPTION, EnhancedMultiplyChargedScan to EMC, TimeDelayedFragmentationScan to TDF, with a comment that these are the values writeTo emits. (2) :1186-1191 the MSn fallback now sets MSNSPECTRUM on spec_, with a comment that the spectrum being parsed is not in exp_ yet and exp_ may be empty. The writer is unchanged, so no on-disk format change and no reference file is affected (0 files contain these values). A shared bidirectional table, as the report proposes, would be a larger refactor than needed. No test added: MzDataFile_test.cpp is not owned (see notes).

The three writer spellings now load as ABSORPTION/EMC/TDF instead of MASSSPECTRUM (MS1) or UNKNOWN with the previous spectrum flipped to MSNSPECTRUM (MSn). Other unknown values on MSn spectra now mark the current spectrum MSNSPECTRUM and leave the previous one alone. No reference mzData file contains such a value. MzDataFile_test.cpp:170-172 expects MASSSPECTRUM, MASSSPECTRUM and SIM from MassScan/MassScan/SelectedIonDetection, which are still handled as before. Writer output is byte-identical.

verdicts.claim: Modifications on residues inside a ModifiedRange, e.g. the oxidation in (M[UNIMOD:35]A)[+1], are parsed and written back out, but resolution, mass validation and mass accumulation all skip them, so the mass silently loses them.
verdicts.evidence: The parser stores the inner modifications (ProForma.cpp:1163, 1169) and the writer emits them (550). At HEAD, resolveModifications' range branch (HEAD 2113-2117) resolved only range->modifications. calculateChainMass_ (HEAD 1958-1966) added only the range's residue masses plus the range-level modifications. getMassCalculationIssues (HEAD 2521-2533) checked only residues plus range-level modifications. So an unresolvable inner modification also went unreported.
verdicts.change: resolveModifications now resolves each range element's modifications with that element's residue (2195-2197). calculateChainMass_ adds them through addModMass (1991), so cross-link counting matches ordinary residues. The mass-issue collector checks them at the element's residue position (2653). toAASequence is unchanged: it still reports MODIFIED_RANGE and does not attach range contents.
verdicts.regression_risk: Masses of ranges with inner modifications grow by those modifications. canCalculateMass/getMonoWeight now reject ranges whose inner modifications cannot be resolved. No existing test or fixture puts modifications inside a range (the range tests at ProFormaParser_test.cpp:333/523 only parse).

verdicts.claim: Mass validation of an ambiguous region compares only the unmodified candidate residue masses and never checks candidate modifications. Accumulation then uses the first candidate, so (?I[UnknownMod999]L) silently drops an unresolved modification and (?I[+10]L) gives a mass that depends on candidate order.
verdicts.evidence: At HEAD, getMassCalculationIssues' AmbiguousRegion branch (HEAD 2506-2520) put only res->getMonoWeight(Internal) into a std::set<double> and never called checkModificationForMass_. calculateChainMass_ (HEAD 1949-1956, unchanged) adds elements[0]'s residue and modifications only. resolveModifications does resolve candidate modifications (2182-2186), so the omission is in validation only.
verdicts.change: The mass-issue collector (now collectMassCalculationIssues_, 2618-2643) runs checkModificationForMass_ on every candidate's modifications. It compares complete candidate masses (residue plus resolvable modification masses, 1e-6 Da tolerance against the first candidate) and reports AMBIGUOUS_REGION when they differ. Accumulation still uses the first candidate, which is now order-independent because every accepted candidate has the same mass. The model is unchanged: (?XY) stays one position.
verdicts.regression_risk: Unmodified regions behave as before: identical residue formulas give identical doubles, and distinct residues differ by more than 1e-6. Regions whose candidates carry unresolvable or mass-changing modifications are now rejected by canCalculateMass/getMonoWeight/tryGetMonoWeight. The issue text changed from 'amino acids' to 'candidates'; no test matches that string.

verdicts.claim: For K[#XL1]//K[+138.068#XL1], the label-only endpoint claims XL1 first, so the linker mass at the other endpoint is skipped. The mass differs by 138 Da depending on chain order.
verdicts.evidence: At HEAD, addModMass (HEAD 1927-1939) inserted alternatives[0]'s CROSSLINK identifier into counted_crosslinks whether or not the bracket carried chemistry. getModificationMass_ returns {true, 0.0} for the empty InfoTag of '[#XL1]' (1925), so the claimed endpoint contributed 0 Da. The later chemistry endpoint then returned early.

A label-only endpoint contributes its 0 Da and no longer blocks the linker. counted_crosslinks became std::map<std::string,double>, so a second chemistry endpoint whose mass differs by more than 1e-3 Da logs OPENMS_LOG_WARN; the first still wins. The label is found on any alternative through the new crossLinkLabel_ helper (1896), matching collectConversionIssues_.
verdicts.regression_risk: Unchanged for the existing tests, which all put chemistry on the first endpoint (ProFormaParser_test.cpp:2638, 2658, 2859, 2926, and the terminal case at 2030). Masses change only where a label-only endpoint came first, or where the label sat on a non-first alternative. A new warning appears for genuinely conflicting endpoint masses.

verdicts.claim: tryGetMonoWeight resolves copy A, then validates a second copy B that getMassCalculationIssues resolves after A interned a Formula tag, and calculates with A. Validation can pass while the calculation silently omits a name that stayed unresolved in A.
verdicts.evidence: At HEAD, tryGetMonoWeight(pf) (HEAD 2642-2647) did copy+resolve, then getMassCalculationIssues(pf_copy), which itself copies and resolves again (HEAD 2491-2492), then calculateChainMass_ on the first copy. resolveFormulaTag_ inserts ModificationsDB entries as a side effect (1665-1700), so the two resolutions can differ. The PeptidoformIon overload and getMonoWeight also validated and calculated different copies.
verdicts.change: The body of getMassCalculationIssues moved into collectMassCalculationIssues_, which works on an already resolved peptidoform (2590). This follows the existing collectConversionIssues_ pattern. getMassCalculationIssues(pf) is now copy+resolve+collect. getMonoWeight(pf) and tryGetMonoWeight(pf) resolve once, then validate and calculate that same copy. The PeptidoformIon overloads use resolveChainsForMass_ (2673), which resolves each chain once, collects prefixed issues, and returns the copies that are then summed.

A forward alias still resolves only from the second call on, but it is reported instead of being silently omitted. Chimeric/empty-chain ordering and exception types are unchanged.

verdicts.claim: For M[INFO:note], the issue collector reports nothing and isRepresentableAsAASequence returns true, but strict toAASequence throws because the attachment loop rejects every null resolved_mod.
verdicts.evidence: The collector (2277-2283) raises UNRESOLVED_MOD only when carriesChemistry_(mod). At HEAD the attachment loop (HEAD 2307-2311) threw ConversionError for any mod with resolved_mod == nullptr under FAIL_ON_LOSS. Any chemistry-carrying unresolved mod has already been rejected by the issue check at 2365, so that throw was reachable only for annotation- or label-only brackets, which is exactly the inconsistent case.

verdicts.claim: The terminal conversion-issue loops never inspect cross-link labels, so strict conversion of a terminal [#XL1] (or linker chemistry with a label) silently returns the sequence without the link.
verdicts.evidence: At HEAD the residue loop raised CROSS_LINK for any CROSSLINK label (HEAD 2206-2212). The N-terminal and C-terminal loops (HEAD 2229-2238, 2251-2260) checked only unresolved chemistry and alternatives. toAASequence attaches the first resolved terminal bracket (2431-2438) and cannot represent a link.

BEST_EFFORT output is unchanged, so the terminal-label test at ProFormaParser_test.cpp:2027 still holds.

verdicts.claim: An empty ambiguous region emits no residue, but the attachment cursor still advances past it. A following modified residue is then set at index 1 of a one-residue AASequence, and AASequence::setModification throws IndexOverflow.
verdicts.evidence: At HEAD, residue emission added elements[0] only for non-empty regions (2376-2378), while the attachment loop did seq_pos++ for every AmbiguousRegion (HEAD 2333). AASequence.cpp:1444-1447 correctly throws IndexOverflow, so nothing needs to change there. parseAmbiguousRegion_ (1118-1144) has no empty-region check, unlike parseModifiedRange_ at 1175, so '(?)' appears to be reachable from text as well.
verdicts.change: The cursor now advances only for a non-empty region (2424-2427), mirroring the emission rule. AASequence.cpp is unchanged: its bounds check was correct.
verdicts.regression_risk: Output changes only for peptidoforms containing an empty ambiguous region: those previously threw under BEST_EFFORT or misplaced later modifications. Non-empty regions are unaffected.

verdicts.claim: When combining modifications on one residue whose diff formulas carry a net charge, the agreement check counts charge*PROTON_MASS_U, but the combined formula is re-interned from toString(), which drops the charge. The result loses a proton mass.

At HEAD, combineOnOneResidue_ (HEAD 1734-1738) took the formula route on mass agreement alone and passed formula_sum.toString() to resolveFormulaTag_. resolveFormulaTag_ itself refuses charged tags (1627, 1638) because ResidueModification has no charge.
verdicts.change: combineOnOneResidue_ takes the formula route only when the summed formula agrees and getCharge() == 0 (1736-1746). A charged sum falls through to the existing mass-only record built from the summed diff masses, so the proton mass is kept. The 'formula disagrees' warning is now limited to real disagreement, and the doc comment names the charge condition. EmpiricalFormula.cpp is unchanged.
verdicts.regression_risk: Only combinations whose summed diff formula has a nonzero net charge change: they become mass-only anonymous modifications instead of Formula-keyed ones. Neutral combinations, including cancelling charges, keep the formula route (tests at ProFormaParser_test.cpp:1819, 1989).

verdicts.claim: Two-chain generateSpectrum takes the linker mass from the endpoint and also lets BEST_EFFORT attach the resolved linker modification to the chain, so the XLMS generator counts the linker twice in the precursor and in linked fragments.
verdicts.evidence: TheoreticalSpectrumGeneratorXLMS.cpp:920-925 and 967-971 compute precursor = alpha.getMonoWeight() + cross_linker_mass + beta.getMonoWeight(). At HEAD, generateSpectrum (HEAD 2820-2833) set cross_linker_mass from findCrossLink and converted unmodified chains with BEST_EFFORT, which attaches every resolved modification (2394-2419). The double count is reachable from text: unimod.xml record 1898 (Xlink:DSS[138], 138.06808 on K) resolves the existing test input 'PEPK[+138.068#XL1]IDE//ANOK[#XL1]THER' (ProFormaParser_test.cpp:3109). The selection rule 'alpha_mass > 0.001' also ignored negative linker masses.
verdicts.change: generateSpectrum now resolves copies of both chains, locates each endpoint with findCrossLink (which returns a CrossLinkEndpoint_ struct), and erases the selected linker bracket from each copy before BEST_EFFORT conversion (2949-2966). Other residue and terminal modifications are kept. The linker mass is passed once, from the endpoint that defines chemistry, whatever its sign (2972). Resolving first gives CV and named linkers their mass. collectPeptidoformIonSpectrumIssues resolves copies too and, via collectCrossLinkIssues_ (2111-2129), reports UNRESOLVED_MOD when an endpoint's linker chemistry has no mass instead of silently using 0 Da. No change is needed in TheoreticalSpectrumGeneratorXLMS.cpp.
