Negative-mass linkers on alpha are now honoured. canGenerateSpectrum(pfi) becomes false for an unresolvable linker. A resolved_mod pointer the caller set by hand is replaced by resolution, as toAASequence already did. The existing test only checks spec.size() > 0.

verdicts.claim: findCrossLink advances its position only for top-level SequenceElements, while BEST_EFFORT conversion flattens ranges (all residues) and non-empty ambiguous regions (one residue). A preceding (AG) range therefore reports alpha position 0 instead of 2.
verdicts.evidence: At HEAD, findCrossLink (HEAD 2017-2041) did ++position only inside the SequenceElement branch. toAASequence emits range->elements.size() residues for a range and one for a non-empty ambiguous region (2372-2382).
verdicts.change: findCrossLink now counts positions exactly as toAASequence emits residues: +1 per SequenceElement, +1 per non-empty AmbiguousRegion, +elements.size() per ModifiedRange (2060-2108). Links are still searched only on top-level residues. A link inside a range or ambiguous region stays 'not found' and is rejected before generation.
verdicts.regression_risk: Only chains with a range or ambiguous region before the link site change their cross_link_position, which shifts XLMS fragment boundaries to the correct residue. Chains made only of plain residues get identical positions.

verdicts.claim: doPopulateSpectraWithData_ guards the decoded peaks length only with assert(), then loops to 2*peaksCount and reads past a shorter payload in release builds.
verdicts.evidence: HEAD MzXMLHandler.cpp:1175 and :1202 had `assert(data.size() == 2 * spectrum_data.peak_count_);`, and the loops at :1177/:1204 ran to `2 * spectrum_data.peak_count_` (unsigned int arithmetic), indexing data[n] and data[n+1]. peak_count_ is a UInt filled from attributeAsInt_ at :301, so peaksCount="-1" wraps to 4294967295. I ran it in a scratch build outside the repo: the HEAD handler compiled with -DNDEBUG and linked against build/build-system-debug/lib/libOpenMS.dylib. peaksCount="2" with a one-pair payload gave a 2-peak spectrum, the second peak read past the vector. peaksCount="-1" crashed with SIGBUS.
verdicts.change: New lines 1199-1211 compute `expected_values = 2 * static_cast<Size>(peak_count_)`, which cannot wrap. A small lambda calls fatalError(LOAD, ...) when the decoded length differs. fatalError logs a message naming the scan, the decoded count and peaksCount, then throws Exception::ParseError. populateSpectraWithData_ already catches exceptions from the parallel loop and rethrows them as ParseError. Both precision branches call the check in place of the assert (1226, 1253), and both loops now stop at data.size(). An empty payload still returns early at line 1190, as before. The comment says the check has to run at runtime because asserts are compiled out of release builds. Scratch check: mismatched 32- and 64-bit payloads now throw ParseError for peaksCount 2, 0 and -1.
verdicts.regression_risk: A file whose decoded payload length is not 2*peaksCount now fails to load with ParseError in every build. Before, debug builds aborted on the assert and release builds silently cut the data short or read out of bounds. This matches the Rust port, which rejects the mismatch. I checked all 8 *.mzXML files under src/tests/class_tests/openms/data: every scan decodes to exactly 2*peaksCount values. Loading all 8 with the HEAD and the fixed handler gave identical output (spectra, peaks, precursors, comments).

verdicts.claim: onCharacters handles every SAX text chunk of <precursorMz> separately: each chunk overwrites the m/z, halves the window width again and re-runs the range filter. <comment> keeps only its last chunk.
verdicts.evidence: In HEAD, onCharacters :567-588 ran asDouble_ on each chunk, called setMZ, halved the lower offset into both offsets and applied the precursor m/z range filter. :589-611 called setComment / setMetaValue("#comment") with only the current chunk. SAX2HandlerAdapter.h forwards every Xerces characters() call directly with no buffering. Xerces splits element text around comments, CDATA sections, PIs and entity boundaries. Scratch run with the HEAD handler: `<precursorMz windowWideness="10">12<!-- b -->3.<![CDATA[45]]></precursorMz>` gave m/z 45 with offsets 1.25/1.25. `<comment>Scan<!-- c --> Comment</comment>` gave ' Comment', and a split instrument comment kept only 'Comment'. The range filter tested the chunk '5' instead of 500 and dropped the wrong scan.
verdicts.change: onCharacters (line 621) now appends precursorMz chunks to the scan's char_rest_. Parsing moved unchanged to a new `</precursorMz>` branch in onEndElement (566-594): it runs asDouble_, setMZ, halves the window once and applies the range filter, only when text was collected, and then clears the buffer. Precursors with no text keep their previous result (m/z 0, lower offset W, upper 0), as in the Rust port. char_rest_ is free at that point because mzXML_3.1_mod.xsd puts precursorMz (:401) before peaks (:490). For files that ignore that order, onStartElement (199-206) decodes an already buffered payload first, so peaks and m/z text do not mix. Comments: a new `<comment>` start branch (516-529) clears the target (scan comment, or the instrument "#comment" meta value), and onCharacters appends chunks (633, 642). A later comment still replaces an earlier one. Scratch results with the fix: m/z 123.45 with offsets 5/5, 'Scan Comment', 'Instrument Comment'. A peaks-before-precursorMz file keeps its 3 peaks and m/z 445.5. The range filter keeps only the 500 m/z scan. A 29-check scratch program passes (the HEAD handler fails 10 checks and then crashes).
verdicts.regression_risk: Precursor text delivered in one chunk (every real file) gives identical results; the HEAD vs fixed differential over the 8 reference mzXML files was identical, and MzXMLFile_test's expectations (101/201/301, offsets 5/10/15, 'Scan Comment', 'Instrument Comment') still hold in the scratch run. Behaviour changes: (1) an empty `<comment/>` after a non-empty one now clears the earlier text instead of leaving it; (2) for files that put <peaks> before <precursorMz>, the payload is decoded on the SAX thread, so a peaksCount mismatch there throws from inside the parse instead of from populateSpectraWithData_ (same exception type).

verdicts.claim: MSDataSqlConsumer owns its handler through a raw pointer: it leaks when the constructor throws after allocating it, and the implicit copy duplicates the owning pointer (double delete).
verdicts.evidence: Original MSDataSqlConsumer.h:94 declared `OpenMS::Internal::MzMLSqliteHandler * handler_` and no copy operations. MSDataSqlConsumer.cpp:18 allocated it in the init list, :22-26 then called reserve() and createTables(), both of which can throw. The only `delete handler_` was in the destructor (:42), and a destructor does not run for a constructor that throws. A copy would have deleted the same handler twice.
verdicts.change: handler_ is now std::unique_ptr<MzMLSqliteHandler> (MSDataSqlConsumer.h:134, <memory> included). The type stays forward-declared, and the constructor and destructor are defined in the .cpp where it is complete. Copy constructor and copy assignment are explicitly deleted (h:61-64). Beyond documenting intent, this stops MSVC dllexport from instantiating an ill-formed implicit copy. The manual delete is gone.
verdicts.regression_risk: The class is no longer copyable. Nothing copies it: its users are OpenSwathBase.cpp and OpenSwathWorkflow.cpp (both through a pointer) and the pyopenms nanobind binding, which only uses nb::init. The member type change alters the class ABI.

verdicts.claim: The MSDataSqlConsumer destructor calls throwing flush/writeRunLevelInformation, so an I/O error escapes a noexcept destructor and terminates the process.
verdicts.evidence: Original MSDataSqlConsumer.cpp:29-43: the destructor called flush() (handler writeSpectra/writeChromatograms) and writeRunLevelInformation(), both of which throw on SQL failure. Destructors are implicitly noexcept, so an escaping exception calls std::terminate. The codebase already has a pattern for this: MSChromatogramParquetConsumer has a public finalize() plus try/catch with logging in its destructor (MSChromatogramParquetConsumer.cpp:191-212, .h:85-90).
verdicts.change: Added a public, idempotent finalize() (h:82-91, cpp:57-69). It flushes both buffers and writes the RUN entry once, guarded by wrote_any_run_. The destructor (cpp:39-55) calls finalize() inside try/catch (std::exception, ...) and reports failures with OPENMS_LOG_ERROR. The header tells callers to call finalize() themselves if they need to handle the error.
verdicts.regression_risk: A write failure during destruction is now logged instead of terminating the program. Files from successful writes are byte-identical, because the same calls run in the same order.

verdicts.claim: addRun/setRunId change the handler's run id without flushing, so records buffered under run A are written under run B.
verdicts.evidence: Original MSDataSqlConsumer.cpp:45-58: addRun and setRunId called handler_->setRunId() directly. flush() (:60-75) then wrote the buffers through writeSpectra/writeChromatograms, which bind the handler's current run_id_ in the INSERTs (MzMLSqliteHandler.cpp SPECTRUM insert `run_id_`, CHROMATOGRAM insert `run_id_`). The only production caller, openswath/src/OpenSwathWorkflow.cpp:1658-1669, calls addRun/setRunId right after construction, when the buffers are still empty. So flushing first is safe, and it matches the documented 'subsequent writes' from the caller's side.
verdicts.change: addRun() and setRunId() call flush() before changing the run id (cpp:73-74, 86-87), with a comment explaining that the buffers do not record their run. The header documents this on both functions (h:93-110).
verdicts.regression_risk: None for OpenSwathWorkflow, whose buffers are empty at those calls. A mid-stream run switch now issues one extra batch insert, and a flush error now surfaces from addRun/setRunId.

verdicts.claim: SpectrumAccessSqMass indexes its subset vector with unchecked (negative or too-large) positions in the nested constructor and both single-spectrum getters.
verdicts.evidence: Original SpectrumAccessSqMass.cpp:43 only checked `indices[k] >= (int)sp.sidx_.size()` before `sp.sidx_[indices[k]]`, so a negative int becomes a huge size_t. :75 `sidx_[id]` in getSpectrumById and :106 in getSpectrumMetaById had no check at all. With an empty sidx_ (full view) the id goes straight to the handler, which throws IllegalArgument when the row count does not match (MzMLSqliteHandler::readSpectra). Only subset views were undefined behaviour.
verdicts.change: Added a file-local storageIndex(sidx, id) (cpp:15-34). It throws Exception::IllegalArgument for id < 0 or id >= sidx.size() before any vector access, and both getters use it (cpp:90, 114). The nested constructor now also rejects negative entries (cpp:63-64). Header @throws docs were updated, including that a parent with no subset defers checking to read time. Tests cover subset positions 1 and -1 for both getters, plus parent-subset -1.
verdicts.regression_risk: Invalid positions now throw IllegalArgument instead of being undefined behaviour. Valid access is unchanged.

verdicts.claim: getAllSpectra passes the subset to SQL IN, so the configured view order is lost and duplicate positions make the handler's size check throw.
verdicts.evidence: Original SpectrumAccessSqMass.cpp:137 passed sidx_ unchanged to handler_.readSpectra. The handler selects `WHERE SPECTRUM.ID IN (...)` and throws if the returned count differs from indices.size(). A read-only sqlite3 probe on SqliteMassFile_1.sqMass gave: `IN (1,0)` returns ids 0,1 (plan: SEARCH USING sqlite_autoindex_SPECTRUM_1), and `IN (1,1)` returns one row. So view [1,0] came back swapped and [1,1] threw, while getSpectrumById honours the position. sqmass-a's working-tree change adds `ORDER BY SPECTRUM.ID` to prepareSpectra_ and populateSpectraWithData_ (CPP-192), which makes the ascending order guaranteed.
verdicts.change: getAllSpectra (cpp:146-168) now sorts and deduplicates sidx_, reads each distinct id once, and rebuilds the configured view with lower_bound, repeats included. If sidx_ is already strictly ascending the read result is used directly, with no extra copy. The header documents that positions keep their order and multiplicity in every accessor. New test: view [1,0,1] returns sizes 19800/19914/19800, and each position's native id and array size match getSpectrumMetaById/getSpectrumById.
verdicts.regression_risk: Output is identical for ascending unique subsets, which covers all existing callers (readSpectraForWindow indices, the existing tests). SpectrumAccessOpenMSInMemory built from an unsorted sqMass view now receives spectra in view order. It still depends on ascending-id results from the handler, which sqmass-a's ORDER BY guarantees.

verdicts.claim: SpectrumAccessSqMass never fills SpectrumMeta::index, so it stays 0 for every spectrum.
verdicts.evidence: Original SpectrumAccessSqMass.cpp:114-117 and :153-156 set id, RT and ms_level only. DataStructures.h:158-159 documents index as the zero-based consecutive index, and the default constructor sets it to 0 (:168-171). No reader in core uses SpectrumMeta::index (grep). SpectrumAccessOpenMS.cpp:82-90 and SpectrumAccessOpenMSCached.cpp:56-64 also leave it 0.
verdicts.change: getSpectrumMetaById sets index to the view position id (cpp:122-123), and getAllSpectra sets it to k (cpp:184). Header docs describe the field. The DataStructures.h index doc now notes that implementations which do not fill it leave it at 0. Tests assert index for the full view, a subset and the reordered view.
verdicts.regression_risk: None known: no code reads the field. Other accessors are not changed.

verdicts.claim: The parent-subset class test builds indices2=[50] but passes the old indices again, so the 50 case is never tested.
verdicts.evidence: Original SpectrumAccessSqMass_test.cpp:101-103: `indices2.push_back(50); TEST_EXCEPTION(..., new SpectrumAccessSqMass(*ptr, indices))`.
verdicts.change: The test now passes indices2 (test:104) and adds a negative case, indices3=[-1] (test:106-108). Before the CPP-207 fix that case was undefined behaviour. New getter sections were added as well.
verdicts.regression_risk: Test-only. The -1 case depends on the CPP-207 constructor check.

verdicts.claim: The SpectrumAccessSqMass header example constructs MzMLSqliteHandler with one argument, but the constructor needs a run id.
verdicts.evidence: Original SpectrumAccessSqMass.h:67 `OpenMS::Internal::MzMLSqliteHandler handler(file);`, while MzMLSqliteHandler.h:59 declares `MzMLSqliteHandler(const std::string& filename, const UInt64 run_id)` with no default.
verdicts.change: The example now reads `MzMLSqliteHandler handler(file, 0); // the run id is only used when writing` (h:69).
verdicts.regression_risk: None (documentation only).

verdicts.claim: filterByDrift has its guards commented out: it dereferences a missing drift-time array and walks intensity/drift iterators to the m/z length unchecked. SqMass spectra never have a drift array.
verdicts.evidence: Original ISpectrumAccess.h:85-92 had the preconditions and the throw commented out. :98-102 took `input->getDriftTimeArray()`, which returns null when absent (DataStructures.h getDriftTimeArray), and dereferenced `im_arr->data` and `im_arr->description`. The loop (:110-121) advanced int_it and im_it once per m/z element. SpectrumAccessSqMass::getSpectrumById builds only m/z and intensity arrays, and sqMass DATA_TYPE covers only mz/int/rt. DIAHelper.cpp:146-151 already throws MissingInformation when IM integration has no drift array.
verdicts.change: filterByDrift (ISpectrumAccess.h:108-139) now throws std::invalid_argument for a null input, a missing m/z or intensity array, a missing drift-time array, or arrays of unequal length. OpenSwathAlgo does not link OpenMS, so std exceptions are used, and <stdexcept> is included. getDriftTimeArray skips null array pointers (DataStructures.h:261-265), so those checks are reachable instead of crashing inside the lookup. Both drift overloads document the throw.
verdicts.regression_risk: Calls that used to segfault (null drift array) or read out of bounds now throw. Spectra with equal-length IM arrays filter exactly as before. A spectrum whose IM array is longer than m/z, previously silently truncated, now throws. TOPPBase catches std::exception.

verdicts.claim: The SqMassFile::store docs say the file is created if necessary, but store always deletes an existing database first.
verdicts.evidence: Original SqMassFile.h:95-97 said 'creating the file (and the required SQLite tables) if necessary'. SqMassFile.cpp:32-33 calls createTables() unconditionally, and MzMLSqliteHandler::createTables begins with std::filesystem::remove(filename).
verdicts.change: store() docs (SqMassFile.h:93-104) now say a new database is written, with an @warning: an existing file is deleted before writing starts, nothing is appended or kept, the replacement is not atomic, and a failed write leaves the old file gone and possibly a partial database. Behaviour is unchanged.
verdicts.regression_risk: None (documentation only).

verdicts.claim: With full_meta, MSDataSqlConsumer discards the supplied ExperimentalSettings, and addRun writes an empty snapshot that suppresses the accumulated metadata.
verdicts.evidence: Original MSDataSqlConsumer.cpp:107: setExperimentalSettings was a no-op, although MzMLFile::transform supplies the settings (MzMLFile.cpp:261). peak_meta_ collects record headers only when full_meta_ is set (:81-84, :95-98). addRun (:45-53) wrote an empty-experiment snapshot and set wrote_any_run_, so the destructor skipped peak_meta_ (:36-40). readExperiment then falls back to the SQL columns for an empty snapshot. A late RUN_EXTRA cannot be written on its own, because the handler's writeRunLevelInformation always inserts the RUN row (PRIMARY KEY). OpenSwathWorkflow uses full_meta=false.
verdicts.change: setExperimentalSettings now stores the settings into peak_meta_ via static_cast<ExperimentalSettings&> when full_meta_ is set (cpp:138-146), the same idiom the handler uses. The snapshot written by finalize() therefore carries them. The addRun limitation is documented on addRun (h:93-102) rather than changed: its snapshot holds only the filename, and reading such a file falls back to the SQL tables. New test: a sample name set through setExperimentalSettings round-trips via MzMLSqliteHandler::readExperiment.
verdicts.regression_risk: Full-meta sqMass files written by this consumer now include the input's experimental settings in RUN_EXTRA. No reference data comes from this path: no TOPP test runs the low-memory mzML to sqMass conversion, and OpenSwathWorkflow uses full_meta=false. addRun behaviour is unchanged.

verdicts.claim: A negative buffer size wraps to SIZE_MAX before reserve(), with no clear invalid-size error. The meaning of 0 is undocumented.
verdicts.evidence: Original MSDataSqlConsumer.cpp:16-26 converted `int flush_after` to `size_t flush_after_`, so -1 became SIZE_MAX and reserve() threw std::length_error after the handler was allocated. With 0, `size() >= 0` flushes every record, and the handler's `sql_it > sql_batch_size_` check (MzMLSqliteHandler writeSpectra) also flushes each record. So 0 is a working immediate-write mode.
verdicts.change: The constructor throws Exception::IllegalArgument for flush_after < 0 before reserve() and createTables() (cpp:24-30), so an existing file is not replaced. setConfig receives the validated int. The header documents that 0 writes every record immediately and documents the @throws. The test checks that the throw leaves the previously written file readable.
verdicts.regression_risk: Negative sizes throw IllegalArgument instead of std::length_error, and now before the target file is deleted. Valid sizes are unchanged.

verdicts.claim: The SpectrumAccessSqMass::getSpectraByRT docs promise [RT-delta, RT+delta], but deltaRT=0 returns the first spectrum at or after RT.
verdicts.evidence: Original SpectrumAccessSqMass.h:171 described the exact interval. SpectrumAccessSqMass::getSpectraByRT forwards deltaRT to MzMLSqliteHandler::getSpectraIndicesbyRT, whose `deltaRT <= 0` branch runs `WHERE RETENTION_TIME >= RT ... LIMIT 1`. An sqlite3 probe on the fixture returns id 1 (RT 0.4738) for RT 0.3. ISpectrumAccess::getMultipleSpectra calls getSpectraByRT(RT, 0.0) and depends on this. SpectrumAccessOpenMS/Cached/InMemory return the same first-at-or-after spectrum for 0.
verdicts.change: Documented the zero-width behaviour, which getMultipleSpectra depends on, in SpectrumAccessSqMass.h (deltaRT param) and in the base ISpectrumAccess.h getSpectraByRT doc. Behaviour is unchanged. New test section: (0.3, 0.2) returns 2 spectra, (0.3, 0) returns [1], (0.5, 0) returns [], and subset [1] with (0.3, 0) returns [0].
verdicts.regression_risk: None in code. The new test pins the handler's zero-width query behaviour.

verdicts.claim: getMultipleSpectra always returns the closest spectrum plus n/2 on each side, so n=0 or negative gives 1 and an even n can give n+1, despite docs calling n the sequence length.
verdicts.evidence: ISpectrumAccess.cpp:39-52 (both overloads identical at :75-88) push the closest spectrum, then for i=1..n/2 push closest-i and closest+i when in range. The old header comment (ISpectrumAccess.h:69-79) called it the 'length of the spectrum sequence'. MRMFeatureFinderScoring.cpp:98-99 enforces only add_up_spectra >= 1 (no odd constraint), and OpenSwathScoring feeds it directly. The class tests use add_up_spectra=1 only. Capping or rejecting even values would change OpenSWATH scoring results for existing even settings.
verdicts.change: Replaced both non-Doxygen comments with @brief/@param docs (ISpectrumAccess.h:79-106). They give the exact rule: closest spectrum first, then up to n/2 neighbours per side, alternating and not RT-sorted; odd n gives at most n, even n at most n+1, values below 2 give only the closest; empty if no spectrum is at or after RT. The drift overload selects the same spectra. Behaviour is unchanged.
verdicts.regression_risk: None (documentation only).

verdicts.claim: Positive-accuracy Numpress linear encoding gives one- and two-value arrays a fixed point of 0, so they decode as NaN. The ordinary estimator is infinite for short all-zero arrays.
verdicts.evidence: Original MSNumpress.cpp:242-245 returned 0 for dataSize < 3 under the false comment that the first two points are stored as floats. encodeLinear (:324-336) actually quantizes data[0] and data[1] with fixedPoint, and decodeLinear divides by it. optimalLinearFixedPoint (:287-289) divides by data[0] or max(data[0], data[1]), giving inf for zeros. MSNumpressCoder.cpp:133-138 falls back only on a negative estimate. A standalone UBSan driver (-fsanitize=undefined,float-cast-overflow) built against the HEAD MSNumpress.cpp: 14 of 24 short-array cases broke (12 decoded to NaN at accuracy 1e-4/0.05, 2 all-zero arrays got an infinite factor), with float-cast undefined behaviour. With the fix: 24/24 exact, no UB.
verdicts.change: optimalLinearFixedPointMass special-cases only dataSize == 0 (MSNumpress.cpp:242-248). Short arrays now get 0.5/mass_acc bounded by the overflow limit, with the existing -1 fallback. optimalLinearFixedPoint divides by 1 for an all-zero one- or two-value array (:288-299), the bound its residual loop already guarantees for longer arrays. MSNumpressCoder.cpp needs no change, since it no longer receives 0 for nonempty in-range data. The decoder is unchanged, so previously written files load as before. Test: a lossy MSDataSqlConsumer round trip of 1- and 2-peak spectra read through SpectrumAccessSqMass (getSpectrumById and getAllSpectra) returns exact finite m/z.
verdicts.regression_risk: Encoded bytes change only for 1- or 2-value linear arrays with positive accuracy, or all-zero ones. I scanned every numpress-linear mzML (2 files), sqMass (1) and .xic parquet (2) reference file under core/src/tests and test-data: none contain such arrays, so no reference files are invalidated. MSNumpressCoder_test uses 4- and 100-value vectors, so its expected strings are unaffected. OpenSWATH chromatogram outputs (sqMass, chrom.mzML, xic, all at 0.05 s accuracy) now keep 1- and 2-point RTs.

verdicts.claim: The mzML writer puts software version, source-file checksum and fraction identifier into double-quoted attributes without escaping them.
verdicts.evidence: Before the change MzMLHandler.cpp:3775 wrote software.getVersion() raw, :3807/:3811 wrote source_file.getChecksum() raw and :5243 wrote exp.getFractionIdentifier() raw, while the neighbouring sourceFile name/location at :3803 already used the file-local writeXMLAttribute_ helper (:39). The same raw interpolation of caller-supplied text existed at :5417 (scan externalSpectrumID) and for every MS:1000786 non-standard data array name (:5596, :5619, :5812, :5994, :6019). A value such as v'&1 with a double quote closes the attribute early and a bare ampersand starts an invalid entity reference, so the file cannot be parsed.
verdicts.change: All of these sites now go through writeXMLAttribute_: software version (MzMLHandler.cpp:3800), SHA-1 and MD5 checksum text (:3832, :3836), fraction identifier (:5268), externalSpectrumID (:5481) and the non-standard array names in the spectrum and chromatogram writers (:5628, :5651, :5844, :6026, :6051). The checksum site has a short comment saying why. Internal ids (so_*, sf_*, dp_*) and CV-derived term and unit names were left alone. Checksum content validation is still a separate matter.
verdicts.regression_risk: Output bytes change only when one of these strings contains an ampersand, angle bracket, quote, apostrophe, CR/LF/TAB or non-ASCII text. Non-ASCII now becomes numeric character references, as the other attributes already do. I grepped every class-test reference .mzML: no software version, fraction identifier, checksum, externalSpectrumID or non-standard array name contains such characters, so no reference output moves. No class test compares written mzML byte for byte.

verdicts.claim: The indexed mzML footer always writes the placeholder fileChecksum 0 instead of a SHA-1 of the preceding bytes.
verdicts.evidence: MzMLHandlerHelper.cpp:130-133 keeps the TODO and writes the constant '0'. share/OpenMS/SCHEMAS/mzML_idx_1_10.xsd (fileChecksum element, around line 1185) documents a SHA-1 from the start of the file to the end of the opening fileChecksum tag. No OpenMS reader checks it: MzMLHandler.cpp only collects its characters and IndexedMzMLDecoder ignores it. The only SHA-1 code is in the anonymous namespace of FileHandler.cpp (around lines 83-174) and is not exposed.
verdicts.change: No change. The correct fix changes on-disk output: wrap the output streambuf of MzMLHandler::writeTo and MSDataWritingConsumer so that every byte written up to and including the opening fileChecksum tag is fed into an incremental SHA-1, then write the 40-hex-digit digest (not hashed itself). That needs the RFC 3174 implementation in FileHandler.cpp moved into a shared helper. All 23 reference documents under src/tests/class_tests/openms/data/ that contain a fileChecksum element carry the placeholder '0' (counted with grep -rl), so this fix would invalidate all 23.
verdicts.regression_risk: None, nothing was changed.

verdicts.claim: An empty indexed mzML declares indexList count 0 but writes a dummy index with offset -1.
verdicts.evidence: MzMLHandlerHelper.cpp:91 gives indexlists = 0 when both offset vectors are empty. The old :97 wrote count 0, then :117-125 wrote one 'dummy' index. The XSD IndexListType.index and IndexType.offset use the default minOccurs of 1 (mzML_idx_1_10.xsd:1119-1154), so once the indexedmzML wrapper is open one index with one offset has to follow. Only MzMLHandler::writeTo with an empty experiment gets here: MSDataWritingConsumer.cpp:166-170 writes a footer only after it has written data, and writeSpectrum_/writeChromatogram_ always add an offset. MzMLFile_test.cpp:1165-1176 requires that storing an empty map with default options still produces the indexedmzML wrapper, so writing plain mzML or throwing for empty input would break that test. IndexedMzMLDecoder.cpp:317-331 already refuses an index named 'dummy', so on-disc access to such a file reports a parse failure.
verdicts.change: The declared count is now the number of index elements actually written, including the dummy: '(indexlists == 0 ? 1 : indexlists)' at MzMLHandlerHelper.cpp:98, with a comment. The placeholder index stays because the schema requires it while the wrapper is written. Dropping the wrapper for empty experiments would mean changing the expectation at MzMLFile_test.cpp:1175 (not owned by this group), so I did not do that.
verdicts.regression_risk: Only empty indexed output changes, from count 0 to count 1. grep finds no reference file with a dummy index or an indexList count of 0. MzMLFile_test only checks for the closing indexedmzML tag. No reader uses the count.

verdicts.claim: Chromatogram loading renames every pressure, flow and detector-signal array to 'intensity array', leaves the selector on the last one while the first becomes the peaks, and drops the rest.
verdicts.evidence: Before the change MzMLHandler.cpp:635-644 looped over all arrays, renamed each physical array to 'intensity array' and overwrote the 'mzml intensity array' selector each time. MzMLHandlerHelper::computeDataProperties_ (MzMLHandlerHelper.cpp:268-281) returns the first array with that name. Supplemental arrays are excluded by name (MzMLHandler.cpp:697/766 before the change), so the other promoted arrays were lost. The writer emits the peak intensities under the stored selector (writeContainerData_ at :5636, term map at :5709-5712). With [time, pressure=200, flow=3] the peaks held 200 but were written as flow. With [time, intensity, pressure] the canonical intensities were written as pressure and the pressure data was dropped.
verdicts.change: populateChromatogramsWithData_ (MzMLHandler.cpp:648-668) promotes a physical array only when no canonical 'intensity array' is present, and then only the first one in document order. The selector is taken from that array alone. Every other array keeps its own name, unit_accession and values and becomes a supplemental float data array, which the writer emits under its own CV term. A comment explains why. This matches how spectra already prefer the m/z array over the wavelength array.
verdicts.regression_risk: A chromatogram with a single physical array (the pressure case in MzMLFile_test.cpp:1455-1496) behaves as before. Chromatograms that combine a canonical intensity array with physical arrays, or have several physical arrays, now keep the extra arrays as float data arrays, and the canonical intensity wins over a pressure array that comes first. No reference mzML contains MS:1000820, MS:1000821 or a 'detector signal' array (grep: 0 files).

verdicts.claim: The numeric Base64 decoders do not check the alphabet or padding, so input such as 16 exclamation marks comes back as numbers.
verdicts.evidence: registerDecoder_ (Base64.cpp:80-114) classifies bytes by upper bounds only, so '!' falls into numberMask. decodeUncompressed_ (Base64.h:309-346 before the change) checked only the length. It is worse on the integer path: decodeIntegersUncompressed_ (old Base64.h:506-561) indexes decoder_[(int)in[i] - 43] with no range check, which reads out of bounds for bytes below '+' or above 'z' (index -10 for '!'), and it had no length-multiple-of-4 check either, so unpadded input read past the end of the string. The existing tests fix some lenient behaviour: decode and decodeIntegers of '====' must give an empty result without throwing (Base64_test.cpp:144-147 and :404-406), decodeStrings of '====' must give one string and 'Q A..A==' must not throw (:300-310). MzDataFile_3_minimal.mzData:34-41 and MzDataFile_4_64bit.mzData hold a 25-byte payload for length=3 doubles, and MzDataFile_test.cpp:448-462 expects those files to load.
verdicts.change: New private helper Base64::checkNumericInput_ (declared at Base64.h:157, defined at Base64.cpp:213). It keeps the old rule that input shorter than 4 characters decodes to nothing and returns false in that case. It throws Exception::ConversionError when the length is not a multiple of 4, a byte is outside the alphabet (checked against the existing decoder_ table, where '$' marks non-Base64 bytes), a data byte follows padding, or there are more than two padding characters. Input made only of padding returns false. It is called by all four numeric decoders: uncompressed and compressed, float and integer (Base64.h:292, :329, :428, :526). This also closes the out-of-bounds table read and the read past the end in the integer decoder. The string decoders are deliberately left unchecked because Base64_test pins their lenient results. A check that the decoded byte count is a multiple of the element size is deliberately not added because it would reject the mzData reference files above. Numpress payloads still go through Base64::decodeSingleString without this check.
verdicts.regression_risk: Malformed numeric Base64 now throws ConversionError where it used to return garbage numbers or read out of bounds. The mzML handlers turn this into ParseError. mzML read with skipXMLChecks=true that has whitespace inside a binary element now fails loudly. I scanned 16613 Base64 payloads in the class-test reference .mzML/.mzXML/.mzData files (after the handlers' whitespace removal) and found no violations. Every Base64_test and MzMLSpectrumDecoder_test input keeps its current outcome. Compressed float input made only of padding now returns empty instead of a zlib error.

verdicts.claim: A spectrum without acquisition info gets a synthetic scan that carries RT but not the spectrum's ion mobility, so its drift time, 1/K0, CCS or FAIMS CV is lost when written.
verdicts.evidence: MzMLHandler.cpp:5424-5459 (before the change) wrote the mobility cvParam only inside the j == 0 branch of the acquisition loop. The fallback branch at :5487-5490 wrote only 'scan start time'. The reader takes spectrum mobility from scan-level cvParams (:2289-2320), so a spectrum with drift time 1.5 ms and empty AcquisitionInfo came back without it.
verdicts.change: The first-scan RT and mobility output (including the FAIMS signed-value rule and the rule that an unset drift time is not written) is now a single local lambda, write_first_scan_rt_and_mobility (MzMLHandler.cpp:5438). Both the first real scan (:5490) and the synthetic scan (:5522) call it, with a comment saying why. The bytes written for real scans are unchanged.
verdicts.regression_risk: Spectra that have no acquisition info but do have a drift time or a FAIMS unit now get the mobility cvParam in their scan element and keep it after a store/load round trip. Spectra without mobility produce identical bytes. No class test compares written mzML against a reference file. In the downstream TOPP test references (not in this repository), tools that write such spectra would gain one cvParam line.

verdicts.claim: MzMLSpectrumDecoder parses records without an error handler, so XML errors are dropped, and the indexed byte range for the last record always includes trailing list/run/mzML end tags.
verdicts.evidence: MzMLSpectrumDecoder.cpp:538-543 (before the change) created a XercesDOMParser without setErrorHandler. The parser stopped at the first fatal error and kept the partial tree. IndexedMzMLHandler.cpp:201-215 and :258-270 end the last record's range at the start of the other list or at index_offset_, and readRecord_ (:34-58) relies on the decoder to reject incomplete records. A test depends on the current silence: MzMLSpectrumDecoder_test.cpp:380-402 feeds a binary element whose text contains a bare '&-', which is ill-formed XML, and expects ConversionError. It only gets that because the parser silently stops at the entity error and the partial Base64 text gets decoded. A handler that throws ParseError would make that test fail.
verdicts.change: Partial fix in the owned file. (1) New recordLength_ (MzMLSpectrumDecoder.cpp:68) finds the leading spectrum or chromatogram start tag, allowing quoted '>' in attributes and empty elements, and its own end tag (so a spectrumList or chromatogramList end tag does not count). Only that record is passed to the parser (:649), so the last record parses as well-formed XML. (2) If the record is not closed within its byte range (truncated input, or an offset that does not point at a record), ParseError is now thrown instead of silently returning partial or empty data. (3) RecordErrorHandler_ (:31) is installed and the first parser error is logged with OPENMS_LOG_WARN (:661). Still pending: throwing ParseError for XML errors inside a closed record. That needs the shared test edit listed in needs_shared_file.
verdicts.regression_risk: Correct indexed files behave as before; the parser just no longer scans the trailing end tags. A record whose range lacks its own end tag now throws ParseError. Every MzMLSpectrumDecoder_test input closes its root element, so every expected outcome stays the same (ParseError, ConversionError, the precondition check, and results). Ill-formed records now also log a warning. Input that does not start with a spectrum or chromatogram tag is passed to the parser unchanged.

verdicts.claim: The mzML list count attributes go straight into reserve(): a negative value wraps to SIZE_MAX (std::length_error) and a huge one allocates before any child is read.
verdicts.evidence: Before the change MzMLHandler.cpp:970/982 did scan_count_total_ = attributeAsInt_(...) followed by exp_->reserveSpaceSpectra(scan_count_total_), which converts Int to Size and calls spectra_.reserve (MSExperiment.cpp:526-529). :1001/:1017 did the same for chromatograms, and :1022 called bin_data_.reserve(attributeAsInt_(...)). StringManager.cpp:109-112 uses XMLString::parseInt, which accepts any signed int. The same untrusted sizing reached memory in the numpress branch of MzMLHandlerHelper::decodeBase64Arrays (MzMLHandlerHelper.cpp:175-186): unlike every other codec branch it did not reset bindata.size to the decoded length. populateSpectraWithData_ reserves by that size (MzMLHandler.cpp:473/483) and copies begin() + min(default_arr_length, data.size) (:558-567), and the chromatogram path indexes floats_64[n] for n < size (:770). A numpress auxiliary array that decodes shorter than its arrayLength was therefore read out of bounds.
verdicts.change: New file-local capacityHint_ (MzMLHandler.cpp:112) returns 0 for a count of zero or less and otherwise at most a limit. It is used for spectra and chromatograms with a limit of 65536 (:1006, :1041) and for bin_data_ with a limit of 16 (:1047; comment: the vector moves into each buffered record together with its capacity). scan_count_total_ and chrom_count_total_ keep the declared value for progress and count reporting. XMLHandler.h and StringManager.cpp are unchanged, since attributeAsInt_ is a general helper where negative values can be legitimate. In the numpress branch of decodeBase64Arrays (MzMLHandlerHelper.cpp:188-195) the declared size is now reset to the decoded length with the same warning the other branches give, which removes the out-of-bounds read.
verdicts.regression_risk: Only reserved capacity changes, not content. Files with more than 65536 spectra or chromatograms grow the vector past the hint by moves. A negative or huge count no longer raises std::length_error or bad_alloc. For numpress arrays whose declared length differs from the decoded one, a warning is now logged and the decoded length is used, as for every other codec. The only reference file with numpress arrays (MSChromatogramParquetConsumer_1_output.chrom.mzML, 36 arrays) has no length mismatch.

verdicts.claim: The streaming mzML consumer writes the header from a one-record dummy map, so a later spectrum's sourceFileRef / dataProcessingRef point to entries the header never declared.
verdicts.evidence: MSDataWritingConsumer.cpp (HEAD) 76-83 builds `MapType dummy; dummy.addSpectrum(scpy); writeHeader_(ofs_, dummy, dps_, ...)` once. MzMLHandler::writeHeader_ declares `sf_sp_<i>` only for spectra in that map (MzMLHandler.cpp ~5003) and pushes only the first spectrum's history into dps (~5108). MzMLHandler::writeSpectrum_ then writes `sourceFileRef="sf_sp_<s>"` for any non-default source file (~5296), and when the history is not pointer-equal to dps[0] it falls back to `dp_ref_num = s` -> `dp_sp_<s>` (~5300-5302). Float-array refs `dp_sp_<s>_bi_<m>` (~5855) are likewise declared for s=0 only. The reader turns these into a warning and a dropped source file (~930) and an empty history via `processing_[ref]` default-insert (~945). The claim holds for any s>=1, even when the source file equals the first one, because the id is index-based.
verdicts.change: In consumeSpectrum, once the header is published (new else branch, MSDataWritingConsumer.cpp 90-125), the copy is reduced to what the header declares. A history that differs by pointer but is equal by content (Helpers::cmpPtrContainer) gets the first spectrum's pointers, stored in the new member first_spectrum_data_processing_; that case loses nothing. A history that differs in content also falls back to the declared default. A later spectrum's own source file and its float-array processing are dropped. OPENMS_LOG_WARN fires once (warned_undeclared_references_) whenever information is lost. I chose this over throwing: throwing would abort streaming of ordinary inputs such as OpenMS's own MzMLFile_1.mzML (spectrum-level sourceFileRef, spectra with dp_sp_2/dp_sp_3) through IndexedMzMLFileLoader::store or OpenSwath split mode, and writeChromatogram_ already gives every chromatogram the default history. Documented as an @note in MSDataWritingConsumer.h. The regression check is in MSDataWritingConsumer_test.cpp [EXTRA]: no dangling refs in the text, and the equal-content history survives read-back.
verdicts.regression_risk: Streamed mzML changes only when a later spectrum had a source file, float-array data processing, or a history that is not pointer-identical to the first spectrum's. Those files used to carry dangling IDREFs. Now the refs are omitted, and a content-different history is replaced by the first spectrum's, with a warning. Files read through MzMLFile::transform share processing pointers, so they are unaffected. IndexedMzMLFileLoader_test input (IndexedmzMLFile_1.mzML: one dp, no spectrum sourceFileRef) is unaffected. No class-test reference mzML is produced by streaming. Adds two members, so the ABI of MSDataWritingConsumer changes.

verdicts.claim: MSDataWritingConsumer_test is not registered and calls a constructor that does not exist, so it gives no coverage.
verdicts.evidence: HEAD MSDataWritingConsumer_test.cpp:27 `new MSDataWritingConsumer()`: the class is abstract (pure virtual processSpectrum_/processChromatogram_, MSDataWritingConsumer.h:154,161) and its only constructor takes a filename (h:76). All other sections are `// TODO`. executables.cmake:239 reads `#MSDataWritingConsumer_test`.
verdicts.change: Rewrote the test against the current API. It uses PlainMSDataWritingConsumer on NEW_TMP_FILE paths and follows the START_SECTION/TEST_EQUAL idiom. Sections: constructor/destructor; setExperimentalSettings (sample name round-trips); setExpectedSize (count attributes); consumeSpectrum (counts, IllegalArgument for a spectrum after chromatograms, read-back); consumeChromatogram; addDataProcessing (added to the written copy only); plus the CPP-172 [EXTRA] regression. A syntax-only compile of the file with the build's flags passed. Re-enabling it needs executables.cmake, which this group does not own (see needs_shared_file).
verdicts.regression_risk: None until registered. Once registered it adds a new test executable that reads back mzML written by the streaming consumer.

verdicts.claim: sql_batch_size_ is never initialised unless setConfig is called, so writes compare against an indeterminate value.
verdicts.evidence: HEAD MzMLSqliteHandler.h:238 `int sql_batch_size_;` has no initializer. The constructor init list (cpp:269-277) stops at write_full_meta_(true). setConfig (h:121-127) is the only assignment. Uses are at cpp:1263 and 1474. MzMLSqliteHandler_test writeExperiment (line 448) and writeSpectra (551) write without setConfig.
verdicts.change: Added `sql_batch_size_(500)` to the constructor init list (MzMLSqliteHandler.cpp:304, in declaration order), matching setConfig's default. Documented the default on @param sql_batch_size. I did not add validation: a non-positive value just flushes after every record, and an oversized one fails at prepare with IllegalArgument (rolled back, see CPP-194).
verdicts.regression_risk: None. Callers that never called setConfig now batch every 500 parameters instead of an arbitrary amount.

verdicts.claim: Blob hydration takes the container length from the first array only, copies later arrays with an unchecked iterator, and counts rows instead of checking roles.
verdicts.evidence: HEAD MzMLSqliteHandler.cpp:199-207 (and 219-227, 238-243): `if (containers[curr_id].empty()) resize(data.size())`, then the loop walks the container while `++data_it` advances through `data` unchecked. A shorter later array is read past its end; a longer one is truncated. `cont_data[curr_id] += 1` with the final check `cont_data[k] < 2` (258) accepts two m/z rows and no intensity row.
verdicts.change: Added an acceptArray lambda in populateContainer_sub_ (cpp:139-159). It makes the first array of a container set its length, requires every array to match that length, and throws IllegalArgument on a duplicate role. cont_data is now a role bitmask (1 = intensity, 2 = m/z or RT), and completeness requires `== 3` (285). This also rejects an empty first array followed by a non-empty second one.
verdicts.regression_risk: Only corrupt or foreign files with mismatched or duplicate arrays now throw instead of UB or truncation. Writer-produced arrays have equal lengths, since mz and intensity are encoded from the same spectrum and numpress linear/slof keep the count. MzMLSqliteHandler/SqMassFile/SpectrumAccessSqMass tests compare exact sizes and are unaffected.

verdicts.claim: Data rows are assigned to containers in SQL encounter order, and neither the metadata queries nor the blob queries have an ORDER BY.
verdicts.evidence: HEAD cpp:130-135 maps the first new SQL id to container 0, and so on. The metadata queries (prepareChroms_ 631-635, prepareSpectra_ 753-757) and the data queries (515-523, 541-550, 563-571, 588-597) have no ORDER BY, so the correspondence depends on each plan. In the full-meta path, containers come from RUN_EXTRA in experiment order. Checked with sqlite3 on a copy of SqliteMassFile_1.sqMass that ORDER BY <table>.ID runs off sqlite_autoindex_* with no temp B-tree.
verdicts.change: Every metadata and data query now ends in ORDER BY SPECTRUM.ID / CHROMATOGRAM.ID (cpp:553, 580, 601, 627, 665, 793). The requirement is documented above populateContainer_sub_: the k-th distinct id is the k-th container, and writers assign ascending ids in experiment order, which RUN_EXTRA also follows. If a metadata row has no DATA rows, the completeness check still throws, so a shifted mapping is never returned. Not covered: a concurrent writer changing the file between the two queries (no shared read transaction). sqMass files are write-once.
verdicts.regression_risk: Result order of readSpectra/readChromatograms/readExperiment is now ID order. For writer-produced files that equals the previous rowid order. Cost is negligible, since the primary-key autoindex already provides the order.

verdicts.claim: Native IDs and peptide sequences are pasted between apostrophes without escaping, so valid text breaks the SQL and crafted text can inject SQL.
verdicts.evidence: HEAD cpp:1169-1170 `run_id_ << ",'" << spec.getNativeID() << "',"`; 1204 and 1425 `",'" << pepseq << "'"`; 1405 chromatogram NATIVE_ID the same way. These batches go through sqlite3_exec (SqliteConnector.cpp:152). Only the RUN path (897-900) was parameterized.
verdicts.change: Each text value is quoted with the existing StringUtils::quote(s, '\'', OpenMS::QuotingMethod::DOUBLE), which doubles apostrophes and wraps the value, the same SQL-literal quoting OpenSwathOSWWriter uses. Call sites: cpp:1287, 1318, 1550, 1564. Verified with sqlite3 that `scan'1` and `x'); DROP TABLE RUN;--` round-trip verbatim with the table intact. A NUL byte still cuts the C-string statement inside the literal, which is a syntax error (IllegalArgument, now rolled back), not injection. Full parameter binding would mean restructuring the batched sqlite3_exec writer.
verdicts.regression_risk: Stored text is unchanged for values without apostrophes. Values with apostrophes, which used to fail, now store verbatim. SqMassFile_test's PEPTIDEK round-trip is unaffected.

verdicts.claim: DATA rows are committed before the metadata transaction and counters advance early, so a metadata failure leaves orphan DATA rows. RUN/RUN_EXTRA and the parts of writeExperiment commit separately.
verdicts.evidence: HEAD writeSpectra: DATA executeBindStatement at 1269/1283 (autocommit) before BEGIN at 1286; spec_id_++ at 1261 inside the loop. writeChromatograms is the same (1480/1494 before 1497, chrom_id_++ 1472). writeRunLevelInformation commits RUN at 899-901, then RUN_EXTRA autocommits at 935. writeExperiment (877-885) calls three public writers, each with its own connection.
verdicts.change: The bodies moved into protected writeRunLevelInformation_/writeSpectra_/writeChromatograms_(SqliteConnector&, ...), declared in the header; they do no transaction handling. The public writers and writeExperiment open one connection, BEGIN, call the helper(s), then END. On any exception they roll back via an anonymous rollbackOpenTransaction (sqlite3_get_autocommit check, ROLLBACK), restore spec_id_/chrom_id_ to their entry values, and rethrow (cpp:916-975, 1152-1173, 1420-1441). writeExperiment is now a single transaction. Documented in the class @note and the counter comment.
verdicts.regression_risk: Public signatures are unchanged. The writes before createTables in the class tests still throw IllegalArgument (missing table), now rolled back. A write that throws no longer advances the ids; previously writeSpectra before createTables left spec_id_ at 2. One large transaction per writeExperiment is faster, and SQLite holds the write lock for its whole duration.

verdicts.claim: product_*/precursor_* indexes are created on DATA instead of PRODUCT/PRECURSOR.
verdicts.evidence: HEAD cpp:1047-1051 `CREATE INDEX product_chr_idx ON DATA(CHROMATOGRAM_ID)` and three more on DATA, duplicating data_chr_idx/data_sp_idx (1036-1037). EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN of prepareSpectra_ on a copy of SqliteMassFile_1.sqMass shows `SCAN PRECURSOR LEFT-JOIN`; with the corrected indexes it becomes `SEARCH PRECURSOR USING COVERING INDEX precursor_sp_idx`.
verdicts.change: Moved the four indexes to PRODUCT(CHROMATOGRAM_ID/SPECTRUM_ID) and PRECURSOR(CHROMATOGRAM_ID/SPECTRUM_ID) (cpp:1139-1145), keeping their names. Not deferred: tables, columns and stored values are unchanged, readers never depend on index definitions, and no test compares a written sqMass schema. One reference file (src/tests/class_tests/openms/data/SqliteMassFile_1.sqMass) carries the old targets; it is only a reader input and stays valid, so it invalidates 0 references.
verdicts.regression_risk: Newly created files have different index targets. Query plans change: readSwathWindows now drives from spec_mslevel_idx into precursor_sp_idx. I emulated the SwathFile.mzML layout (114 spectra, 5 windows) with the old and the new indexes; readSwathWindows, readMS1Spectra and readSpectraForWindow return the order MzMLSqliteSwathHandler_test expects (412.5 first; ids 0..108 and 1..109).

verdicts.claim: readSpectraForWindow selects chromatogram precursors too and stops at the first NULL SPECTRUM_ID.
verdicts.evidence: HEAD MzMLSqliteSwathHandler.cpp:92-95 selects `SPECTRUM_ID FROM PRECURSOR WHERE ISOLATION_TARGET BETWEEN ...`, and the loop at 101 treats a NULL column 0 as end of results. writeChromatograms stores PRECURSOR rows with CHROMATOGRAM_ID only, and writeExperiment writes chromatograms first (MzMLSqliteHandler.cpp HEAD 883-884). sqlite3 emulation with a chromatogram precursor at 412.5 ahead of the spectrum rows: the old loop returns 0 ids, the new query returns all 19.
verdicts.change: The WHERE clause now filters `SPECTRUM_ID IS NOT NULL` (cpp:106), and the loop uses Sql::nextRow instead of a NULL sentinel (see CPP-203). The header states that chromatogram precursors are skipped.
verdicts.regression_risk: Only files with chromatogram precursors inside a window change, and they return more ids. MzMLSqliteSwathHandler_test data has no chromatograms.

verdicts.claim: The readSwathWindows doc promises one entry per distinct centre, but DISTINCT applies to the whole (centre, lower, upper) tuple.
verdicts.evidence: HEAD MzMLSqliteSwathHandler.h:57 says 'one SwathMap entry per distinct precursor isolation centre'. cpp:30-33 `SELECT DISTINCT(ISOLATION_TARGET), TARGET-LOWER, TARGET+UPPER`: the parentheses do not scope DISTINCT, so equal centres with different widths give separate rows.
verdicts.change: Documented the tuple semantics: two windows with the same centre and different widths are two entries, and readSpectraForWindow returns the same spectra for both because it only uses the centre. The query's DISTINCT is unchanged, since tuple results are meaningful for variable-width windows. Precursors with a NULL centre are skipped (part of the CPP-203 loop change).
verdicts.regression_risk: None for writer-produced files, whose precursor m/z is never NULL.

verdicts.claim: createTables recreates the database but keeps spec_id_/chrom_id_ from the deleted file.
verdicts.evidence: HEAD cpp:939-1023 removes the file and creates tables and indexes but never touches spec_id_/chrom_id_, which only the constructor sets (271-272). The header counter comment (h:223-230) ties the ids to one database file. SqMassFile::transform selects ids 0..count-1. MzMLSqliteHandler_test writeExperiment (453-462) recreates through the same handler but only checks counts.
verdicts.change: After createIndices_() succeeds, createTables sets both counters to 0 (cpp:1108-1114). If creation throws they are left as they were. Doc notes added to createTables and to the counter comment.
verdicts.regression_risk: Ids in files written after a repeated createTables start at 0 again. Class tests check counts and read by encounter/ID order, which holds either way. MSDataSqlConsumer and SqMassFile::store call createTables once per handler.

verdicts.claim: The activation-method readers exclude only -1, so -2 and lower are cast into ActivationMethod.
verdicts.evidence: HEAD cpp:709-713 and 853-857: `!= -1 && < SIZE_OF_ACTIVATIONMETHOD`, then static_cast into the set. Downstream, Precursor::getActivationMethodsAsString indexes `NamesOfActivationMethod[static_cast<size_t>(m)]` (Precursor.cpp:124), an out-of-bounds read for a negative value. sqlite3_column_int also truncates larger 64-bit values into the valid range.
verdicts.change: Both readers now read sqlite3_column_int64 and insert only when 0 <= value < SIZE_OF_ACTIVATIONMETHOD (cpp:739-749, 889-897). As before, -1 and other out-of-domain values mean 'no method', keeping the existing forward-compatible handling of values at or above the upper bound.
verdicts.regression_risk: None for writer-produced values (-1 or valid enum values).

verdicts.claim: SqMassFile::transform runs an extra empty batch for 0 records and for exact multiples of 500.
verdicts.evidence: HEAD SqMassFile.cpp:52 and 74 `batch_idx <= count / batch_size` leaves idx_start == idx_end, so indices is empty. readSpectra/readChromatograms have OPENMS_PRECONDITION(!indices.empty()) (MzMLSqliteHandler.cpp:422/447). Without assertions, prepareSpectra_ drops the WHERE for empty indices and returns every record, so the `indices.size() != exp.size()` check throws IllegalArgument when count is 500, 1000 and so on. getNrSpectra/getNrChromatograms, each opening the file, were also re-evaluated in the loop condition.
verdicts.change: Counts are taken once and reused for setExpectedSize. The loops run `for (idx_start = 0; idx_start < count; idx_start += batch_size)` with Size arithmetic (SqMassFile.cpp:47-95); <algorithm> added.
verdicts.regression_risk: None. Same batches and order for all other counts, and no empty reads. SqMassFile_test does not exercise transform (no regression test possible in an owned file).

verdicts.claim: setConfig promises write_full_meta allows complete recovery of the input file, but auxiliary data arrays are lost.
verdicts.evidence: HEAD MzMLSqliteHandler.h:116 '(allows complete recovery of the input file)'. writeRunLevelInformation copies each record with clear(false) (cpp:914/920), and MSSpectrum::clear clears the float/string/integer arrays whatever the flag (MSSpectrum.cpp:206-213); MSChromatogram::clear does the same. DATA stores only data_type 0/1/2 (cpp:1236-1260).
verdicts.change: Rewrote @param write_full_meta: settings and all spectrum/chromatogram metadata are recovered, but only m/z-or-RT and intensity arrays are stored, so float/integer/string arrays (e.g. ion mobility) are lost, and lossy compression limits peak precision. Added a sentence to the class description. No behaviour change.
verdicts.regression_risk: None (comments only).

verdicts.claim: Read accessors open with the default READWRITE_OR_CREATE mode, so reading a missing path creates an empty database and reports a missing-table error.
verdicts.evidence: SqliteConnector.h ctor default is `SqlOpenMode::READWRITE_OR_CREATE`, and openDatabase_ passes SQLITE_OPEN_CREATE (SqliteConnector.cpp:66-67). HEAD readers use `SqliteConnector conn(filename_)`: MzMLSqliteHandler.cpp 282, 366, 396, 421, 440, 457, 499 and MzMLSqliteSwathHandler.cpp 26, 61, 89.
verdicts.change: All ten read paths now pass SqliteConnector::SqlOpenMode::READ_ONLY (MzMLSqliteHandler.cpp 312, 396, 426, 451, 470, 487, 529; MzMLSqliteSwathHandler.cpp 39, 73, 98). A missing file now raises SqlOperationFailed from open and leaves no file behind. Write and create paths keep the creating mode. Documented in the MzMLSqliteHandler class notes and the SWATH constructor doc. SqliteConnector.cpp needs no change.
verdicts.regression_risk: Reading a nonexistent sqMass now throws SqlOperationFailed where it used to throw IllegalArgument, and no longer creates a zero-byte file. No class test reads a missing file. The reference sqMass uses a rollback journal (journal_mode=delete), so read-only opens work.

verdicts.claim: The SWATH accessors ignore sqlite3_step return codes and treat a NULL column as end of results, so a step error becomes a successful empty result or prefix.
verdicts.evidence: HEAD MzMLSqliteSwathHandler.cpp:40/49, 70/75 and 99/104 discard sqlite3_step's result, and 42, 72, 101 loop `while (sqlite3_column_type(stmt,0) != SQLITE_NULL)`. sqlite3_finalize's result is also ignored (53, 79, 108).
verdicts.change: Each loop now uses the existing Sql::nextRow (SqliteConnector.cpp:243-272), which returns ROW/DONE and throws SqlOperationFailed on any other status.
